issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Propose **BiomniBench-DA public-50 with five derived-input variants** as a candidate in-distribution (ID) development evaluation for Marin. Review the protocol and collect external-model evidence before deciding whether to add it to the ID policy. No Marin models, including Snowball, will be evaluated until that policy decision.

Use Marin's standard evaluation launcher and the selected BixBench harness/judge settings, while retaining Biomni's tasks, grading rubrics and 60-minute agent budget. Our Daytona eval account rejects the authors' 16 GiB RAM / 20 GiB disk requests, so the proposal caps resources at 8/10 GiB and documents the affected inputs. This is a modified public-subset protocol; it does not reproduce the paper's full-benchmark scores.

The Qwen control task (`da-4-6`) completed with a signed score of 28/100 and unsigned comparison of 38/100. Both required reports and the graded verifier result were read back from the archive. EvalDash's API reports continuous reward 0.28 with 1/1 scored coverage; visual rendering and independent audit of the judge's decisions remain pending. The remaining three pilot cases are in image preparation; full baselines remain pending.

## Description

[BiomniBench-DA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235) contains biomedical data-analysis tasks requiring executable analysis and written reports. Use all 50 public tasks at revision `e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235`, retaining the five modified-input tasks in the denominator. The [paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.12.724604v2.full) reports aggregates over 100 tasks and three repetitions. We have not found author scores for the public 50 or saved per-task judgments that establish scoring parity.

The evaluation would measure multi-step analysis and reporting for ID development. Its incremental value beyond BixBench still needs evidence: task-content comparison alone does not establish different model rankings or useful checkpoint-selection signals. This proposal follows the external-baseline and evidence pattern in [SimpleQA Verified #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).

The existing [task-content comparison with BixBench public 205](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6781595235) reviews all 50 BiomniBench prompts/input descriptions, all 205 BixBench questions and 12 selected BiomniBench rubrics. It identifies candidate additional coverage in censored survival analysis, TCR repertoire interpretation, cell–cell communication, gene co-expression networks and chromatin analysis. Its manual inventory labels 27 tasks as substantially overlapping, 11 as extensions and 12 as distinctive workflows; these are granularity-dependent judgments, not a measured redundancy rate. The comparison motivates this proposal but does not establish different model rankings, reliable grading or feasibility of the five modified-input tasks.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Determine whether the public tasks remain valid under the disclosed resource and input changes, whether scoring is reproducible and auditable, and whether the benchmark adds useful coverage beyond BixBench.

Review requested:

- Are the resource/input changes and signed-penalty scoring acceptable for an ID proposal, subject to validation below?
- What additional evidence is needed to establish value beyond BixBench?
- Confirm implementation placement before policy adoption. The pilot uses the existing Harbor path; TaskCompendium/TaskSpec migration is deferred during protocol investigation. That does not establish an exception to the guidance that new evaluation implementations belong in TaskCompendium.

## Proposed protocol

| Component | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Population | All 50 public tasks; no exclusions based on model performance. Report the aggregate and separate 45 unchanged-input / five derived-input summaries. |
| Sandbox | Daytona; preserve each task's native CPU/GPU allocation (2 CPUs, no GPU); RAM = min(native, 8 GiB), disk = min(native, 10 GiB). The release requests 16/20 GiB for 48 tasks and 4/10 GiB for two. |
| Time limits | 3,600 seconds for the agent; 900 seconds for the verifier. Setup and serving startup are separate. |
| Harness | Pi through Marin's standard launcher and vendored Harbor. Pilot pin: Pi 0.87.0. The selected BixBench YAML does not pin Pi; the final baseline version still needs agreement. |
| Context/output | BixBench policy's 65,536 context / 16,384 per-response output settings, with its compaction behavior and model-specific reasoning settings. Verify effective requests. |
| Judge | MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, using the selected BixBench campaign's dedicated-server configuration. Preserve Biomni's rubric and grading prompt. |
| Judge request | Pilot candidate: temperature 0, 8,192 output tokens, 120-second request timeout, no SDK retries; outer verifier limit 900 seconds. These are explicit Biomni pilot settings, not a claim of identical BixBench request settings. |
| Baselines | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B first, then Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and GPT-OSS-20B. Use pinned campaign configurations and record effective reasoning settings. No Marin/Snowball models. |
| Attempts | Pilot: one attempt, no automatic trial retries. Proposed full baseline: three independent solver repetitions per task, subject to protocol and compute-budget agreement. Agree on uncertainty estimation and invalid-output/timeout/recovery rules before launch. Operational retries and judge-only recovery are not independent repetitions; do not take a best-of score. |
| Concurrency | One trial for the initial control; two proposed for the four-case pilot. Concurrency is an operational setting. |
| Evidence | Preserve per-task submissions, trajectories, judge responses, rubric decisions, failures and provenance; validate continuous-score reporting through EvalDash. |

The pilot uses Marin commit `246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7`, with local adapter/preparation files and a bundle-inclusion change. It is not an unchanged main-only execution. Freeze the complete source, image and input manifests for baseline runs. The copied Qwen configuration pins model revision `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`; remaining baseline revisions must be recorded before their runs.

## Changes from the release

Live create requests against the Daytona eval account rejected 16 GiB RAM and 20 GiB disk with explicit per-sandbox maxima of 8 GiB and 10 GiB. These are verified account constraints, not universal Daytona limits. The current choice is the closest supported allocation on this account without requesting a limit increase.

| IDs | Change | Reason and validation required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01–M02 | For `da-1-3` and `da-1-4`, omit the approximately 19.18 GB expression matrix `GSE236581_counts.mtx`; retain clinical and cell metadata. | The matrix exceeds the disk limit. Verify that retained data supports every rubric requirement; expression-based annotations can no longer be rederived. |
| M03–M05 | For `da-17-1`, `da-17-3` and `da-17-5`, replace the approximately 12.22 GB lupus H5AD with the pinned 2.64 GB raw-count derivative. | Preserve all cells and required metadata within the disk limit. Validate gene/cell/donor alignment and task-specific feasibility; normalized expression and embeddings are absent. |
| M06–M07 | Disclose the five input changes in task instructions and remove copies of deliberately omitted files from image recipes. | Prevent assumptions about unavailable data; retain exact prompt/recipe diffs and file hashes. |
| M08 | Existing adapter normalizes `da-20-3`'s 72 JSON-form Docker `COPY` entries to a directory copy. | Historical workaround for Daytona Dockerfile parsing. Apply only if needed by the prepared-image path; verify identical paths and bytes with no extra files. |
| M09 | Cap RAM/disk at 8/10 GiB; preserve smaller native requests and native CPU/GPU. | The confirmed account ceilings reduce the computational budget. Record requested/enforced resources and OOM/disk failures; input fit alone does not prove analysis feasibility. |
| M10 | Replace the release's judge provider implementation with the selected MiniMax judge through Marin's verifier connection. | Align judge model/serving with the selected BixBench campaign. This can change grading decisions and requires auditing. |
| M11 | Apply signed rubric penalties; retain an unsigned comparison score from the same decisions. | The written rubric includes negative points that the released parser drops. This is an intentional scoring change. |
| M12 | Require complete, unique criterion judgments with valid levels/reasons; reject malformed or truncated judge responses. | Treat grader failures as unscored, rather than silently accepting incomplete grades. Error and recovery rates can differ from the release. |
| M13 | Prepare digest-pinned images with Pi/verifier dependencies; adapt verifier connection variables and export continuous `reward`. | Required by the current Marin path. The control image needed a separate data layer to restore its original input at its original path; runtime checksum validation passed. Preserve build recipes, package versions and hashes. |

If any modified task cannot support a required rubric criterion, that blocks the full-50 protocol. Restore sufficient inputs/resources or seek review of a revised protocol before running full baselines; do not count input-induced impossibility as model failure or silently exclude the task.

<details>
<summary>Lupus derivative construction and provenance</summary>

The lupus derivative retains `obs`, `raw` and `uns`, rebuilds `var` from `raw.var`, and links root `X` to `raw.X`. It retains all cells; it is not cell subsampling. Both `X` and `raw.X` contain raw counts. Other root groups, including the original normalized matrix and embeddings, are omitted. The original container filename is retained.

- [Pinned derivative](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83): revision `60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83`, file `lupus-raw-counts.h5ad`, 2,642,705,030 bytes.
- Derived SHA-256: `33179d1cf993091dc0bd41372629534f6b7da1ce1114d74c36110ffbee375d53`.
- Original SHA-256: `7ba85edbdc033a9aeeecabe7a1cfcb0660282cc24b04f49fb52dd3825052c620`.
- These values come from the existing adapter. Rehash downloaded bytes before use; preserve the conversion recipe, source attribution and license. Record the CRC matrix's source hash and all prepared-file hashes in the final manifest.

</details>

## Scoring and failure handling

Preserve `/app/trace.md`, `/app/answer.txt` and the source rubrics. The judge reads agent-authored reports; it does not independently verify every reported action. Audit sampled judgments against the captured tool trajectory.

For each task, sum signed rubric points, retain the raw total, and clamp to `[0, 100]`. Average the clamped per-task scores. Thus a raw −5 is reported as zero, and a reliability penalty of −10 reduces otherwise perfect work from 100 to 90. The released parser's unsigned calculation would yield 100 in the latter case. Neither calculation is established as the one used for the paper's results.

Export `reward = score / 100` for Marin's continuous metric path, preserving the 0–100 score, raw signed total and unsigned comparison in the evidence. Verify EvalDash's displayed scale; report mean rubric score, not accuracy.

The selected runner does not yet guarantee this failure contract: with no exception and a present `verifier_result`, `_read_trial` marks the trial scored even when `rewards.reward` is missing, defaulting its value to zero ([source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L207-L233)). This is confirmed by code inspection, not an end-to-end control. Add missing, nonnumeric and nonfinite reward controls alongside a valid zero; verify scored coverage as well as the aggregate. Resolve any demonstrated adapter/shared-runner defect in a scoped PR before full baselines.

Proposed failure handling:

- Confirmed empty submissions receive zero; grade partial submissions and flag them. Confirm emptiness only after successful inspection of the stopped agent's output location and successful collection. Missing files in an incomplete archive do not establish emptiness. Distinguish confirmed empty output from collection failure in result metadata before full baselines.
- Setup, collection and judge failures remain unscored. Failure to collect a report is not evidence that the report was empty.
- On agent timeout, establish that the agent stopped before capturing and grading its submission. This behavior still needs live validation for the selected runtime.
- Judge-only recovery reuses the same saved submission, rubric and judge settings; retain both original and recovery records. Record any solver rerun separately.
- Report graded coverage and all failures. An incomplete scored-task mean is not a complete 50-task score. Resolve retry/invalid-output rules before full baselines: the paper specifies a retry for invalid/missing output and then zero, which differs from the current pilot's zero retries and proposed unscored infrastructure failures.

Preserve the source instructions' paper-lookup restrictions. Record network access and installed packages; the current environment permits runtime installation and does not fully pin transitive dependencies. The unchanged-input group still shares resource, harness, judge and scorer changes; its score is not native-protocol parity.

## Status

Evidence collected on 2026-11-13:

| Check | Result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Resource limits | Live requests confirmed the eval account's 8 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk ceilings. |
| Scorer replay | Local controls reproduce signed 100/95/90 versus unsigned 100/100/100 for reliability levels A/B/C. These are synthetic judgments, not model scores. |
| Empty submission | An intentionally empty local submission directory emits zero and makes no judge call. The current `missing_submission` label does not itself distinguish confirmed emptiness from failed collection; this control does not validate remote collection-failure handling. |
| Control environment (`da-4-6`) | Remote validation passed for Pi, Python/R, verifier dependencies, the original input checksum and sandbox closure. This does not validate the other 49 tasks or live judging. |
| Standard launcher | Qwen control completed: 28/100 signed, 38/100 unsigned, both reports preserved, verifier status `graded`, 1/1 scored and no recorded trial errors. EvalDash API readback agrees (reward 0.28, continuous metric); this is one control task, not a benchmark-wide score. |
| Remaining execution | Four-case validation (`da-4-6`, `da-1-3`, `da-17-3`, `da-20-3`) and full-50 baselines remain pending. All five derived-input tasks require checks before a full baseline. |

<details>
<summary>Preparation failures and repairs</summary>

Early image preparation failed on an interactive package-install prompt and then on a missing input file; both were repaired before the control evaluation was submitted. A local transport check timed out; the remote worker check subsequently passed. Preserve these negative records in the evidence package. They are not solver failures or zero scores. Historical Luna/GLM diagnostic scores use different settings and will not be pooled into the proposed baselines.

</details>

Before requesting ID adoption:

- [ ] Freeze the final protocol and a 50-row task manifest recording original/derived input hashes, image digests, rubric feasibility, requested/enforced resources and model/Pi/judge revisions. Agree on the proposed three independent solver repetitions and compute budget separately from infrastructure retries and judge recovery. Proposed reporting: mean each task across repetitions, then average tasks equally; report per-repetition means and a task-cluster bootstrap interval, preserving repetitions within each resampled task. Label this as task-sampling uncertainty, not a complete estimate of solver or judge variability.
- [ ] Verify transformed inputs and rubric feasibility for all five affected tasks; validate packaging, enforced resources and task-specific disk/memory use.
- [ ] Exercise good, wrong, partial, confirmed-empty, malformed-judge, missing/invalid-reward and collection-failure controls, plus timeout capture and judge-only recovery; verify coverage and continuous-score display, and audit live judgments against tool traces.
- [ ] Complete external-model public-50 baselines with per-task scores, coverage, 45/five subgroup summaries, failure rates and the agreed uncertainty analysis.
- [ ] Attach the exact pilot patch, preparation recipes and compact validation records; the linked base commit alone does not reproduce the locally modified pilot.
- [ ] Verify archived results and EvalDash ingestion/display; attach reviewable evidence links. Local records are prepared, but a published evidence package is pending.
- [ ] Report wall time, startup/queue time, tokens, sandbox/GPU use, retries, cleanup and measured cost where available. Separate estimates from measurements.
- [ ] Assess incremental coverage beyond BixBench using matched external-model results and documented protocol differences. Reuse suitable existing BixBench evidence where available; additional runs require a separate agreed plan. Three model rankings alone are limited evidence and do not establish checkpoint-selection value. Resolve implementation placement and ownership with evaluation maintainers before the policy decision.

## Links

- [Biology evaluation tracking #9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- [Existing adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) and [adapter source at inspected revision](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/95a4b88b54cae602ade6e79d9536a2c766657301/adapters/biomnibench-da/src/biomnibench_da).
- [Selected BixBench policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/bixbench-pi.yaml) and [MiniMax judge configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/judge-model-configs/MiniMaxAI-MiniMax-M3-MXFP8.yaml).
- [External-baseline evidence precedent #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).
- [Graded Qwen control in EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9). Scorer investigation and complete pilot provenance package: pending attachment before an adoption request.

## Decision Log

Agreed for this investigation: public-50 scope, disclosed resource/input changes, signed scoring with an unsigned comparison, and external baselines starting with Qwen. No Marin-model evaluation before the ID policy decision.

Still open before full baselines: final runtime pins, independent repetitions, uncertainty estimation and failure/recovery rules. Implementation placement, ownership and adoption remain maintainer decisions.

## Conclusion

One control task has completed end-to-end grading and EvalDash API ingestion. There is not yet evidence sufficient to recommend ID adoption. The next decision is whether the proposed deviations and validation plan are acceptable for that assessment.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Daytona agent commands can fail with `ENOENT` or `uv_cwd` after task setup deletes and recreates the image's working directory.

Reproduce:
1. Create a Daytona sandbox whose image uses `WORKDIR /testbed`; leave the machine spec's workdir unset.
2. During setup, delete `/testbed` and recreate it at the same path.
3. Run a new agent command without an explicit command cwd, for example `python3 -c "import os; print(os.getcwd())"` or `pi --version`.
4. Observe a deleted current directory instead of the recreated `/testbed`.

Expected: each new command opens the current directory at the image's logical workdir path.

Main `f5d3c85f9e` passes `command.cwd or self.spec.workdir or None` to Daytona. With both fields unset, the provider can retain the deleted directory. A local process regression covers deletion and recreation, and a regional Linux trial passed with the repair. #11205 fixed control-command output collection; this issue concerns agent-command startup after that fix.

Source: [Daytona command cwd](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L230). The evidence establishes stale cwd behavior; the exact long-lived provider process retaining the inode was not captured.

**Relevant code**
- [`machine.py#L230`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7e6db4032f/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L230) — process-session cwd.

Resolve the image's default workdir when the sandbox starts, before setup can replace it, and use that path for commands without an explicit cwd. Extend the local process regression to recreate an inherited image workdir and verify the next command.

issues.author: RohithKuditipudi
issues.body:
With vLLM on TPU, `LLM.generate` returns corrupted completions when more requests are in flight than the KV cache can hold. The call returns normally and logs no error. Greedy decoding of 256 prompts of about 960 tokens with `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` on one chip gives 13 to 17 completions that are invalid Python. The same prompts decoded 32 at a time give none.

The cache size decides whether it happens. A v6e chip (31 GiB) reaches it at default settings. A v5p chip (96 GiB) reaches it once `gpu_memory_utilization` limits the cache to the same size. A batch job is affected when its in-flight prompts and outputs exceed the cache.

| TPU | KV cache | Invalid Python, 32 at a time | Invalid Python, all 256 at once |
|---|---|---|---|
| v6e-4, defaults | 112,896 tokens | 0 of 256 | 17 of 256 |
| v5p-8, defaults | 598,784 tokens | 0 of 256 | 0 of 256 |
| v5p-8, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.30` | 112,640 tokens | 0 of 256 | 13 of 256 |

Reproduce:
1. On a TPU VM with vLLM `0.20.1rc1.dev0+g70ea9ae8f.tpu`, tpu-inference `0.29.0`, jax and jaxlib `0.11.0`, and libtpu `0.0.50`, save the script below as `kv_cache_repro.py`.
2. On v6e, run `python kv_cache_repro.py --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`.
3. On v5p, add `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30`.

The script uses one chip with `tensor_parallel_size=1`, `max_model_len=8192` and prefix caching off. It prints how many completions fail `ast.parse` for each grouping. We ran it with the same weights loaded from GCS through `--load-format runai_streamer`.

Expected: both groupings give valid completions. A request that does not fit in the KV cache waits, or is recomputed without a change to its output.

One prompt from the v6e-4 run, decoded both ways:

```python
# 32 at a time
    even_count = 0
    odd_count = 0
    for number in numbers:
        if number % 2 == 0:
            even_count += 1
        else:
            odd_count += 1
    return (even_count, odd_count)

# all 256 at once
    even_count = 0
    odd_count = 0
    for number in numbers:
        if number % 2 == 0:
                                  even_count += 1
        else:
!            odd_count += 1
    return (even_count, odd_count)
```

Other observations:
- The output is deterministic. A repeat run corrupts the same completions in the same way.
- The corrupted completions are consecutive requests: positions 100 to 107 and 204 to 219 of 256 on the v6e-4. The cache holds about 110 of these prompts, so these are the last requests admitted in each wave.
- The stray `!` is token id 0 in this tokenizer.
- Sampling at temperature 0.4 shows the same corruption on another set of code prompts, with and without `top_k`.
- `jax.lax.top_k` on one v6e chip returned correct values and indices for 64,000 random rows.
- With the 598,784-token cache, 56 of 256 greedy completions differ between the two groupings and all are valid Python. A text comparison between groupings therefore does not isolate this bug.

The faulty component is not identified. The default log level prints no preemption message, so we have not confirmed that the scheduler preempts requests in these runs.

#6136 reports decode corruption that also depends on the number of concurrent sequences, with a different model and a multi-host setup.

<details>
<summary>kv_cache_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Greedy completions are corrupted once vLLM's KV cache is exhausted (TPU backend).

Decodes the same prompts greedily in one engine, first in groups small enough
to fit the KV cache and then all at once, and counts completions that are no
longer valid Python.

    python kv_cache_repro.py --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct [--gpu-memory-utilization 0.30]
"""
import argparse
import ast
import os

os.environ.setdefault("TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("TPU_PROCESS_BOUNDS", "1,1,1")
os.environ.setdefault("TPU_CHIPS_PER_PROCESS_BOUNDS", "1,1,1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

NUM_PROMPTS = 256
SMALL_GROUP = 32
FILLER_FUNCTIONS = 28  # about 1,000 prompt tokens
STOP = ["\ndef ", "\nclass ", "\n#", "\nif __name__", "\nprint"]


def make_prompt(i: int) -> str:
    lines = ["import math", ""]
    for j in range(FILLER_FUNCTIONS):
        k = i * 1000 + j
        lines += [
            f"def helper_{k}(x, y):",
            f'    """Return x * {j + 2} + y - {k % 97}."""',
            f"    return x * {j + 2} + y - {k % 97}",
            "",
        ]
    lines += [
        f"def count_evens_and_odds_{i}(numbers):",
        '    """Return a tuple (number of even values, number of odd values) in numbers."""',
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def parses(prompt: str, completion: str) -> bool:
    try:
        ast.parse(prompt + completion)
    except SyntaxError:
        return False
    return True


parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
parser.add_argument("--load-format", default=None)
parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=None)
args = parser.parse_args()

kwargs = {"max_model_len": 8192, "enable_prefix_caching": False, "seed": 0, "tensor_parallel_size": 1}
if args.load_format is not None:
    kwargs["load_format"] = args.load_format
if args.gpu_memory_utilization is not None:
    kwargs["gpu_memory_utilization"] = args.gpu_memory_utilization
llm = LLM(model=args.model, **kwargs)
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=256, stop=STOP)
prompts = [make_prompt(i) for i in range(NUM_PROMPTS)]


def decode(group_size: int) -> list[str]:
    texts = []
    for start in range(0, NUM_PROMPTS, group_size):
        texts += [out.outputs[0].text for out in llm.generate(prompts[start : start + group_size], params)]
    return texts


in_groups = decode(SMALL_GROUP)
all_at_once = decode(NUM_PROMPTS)
broken_in_groups = [i for i in range(NUM_PROMPTS) if not parses(prompts[i], in_groups[i])]
broken_all_at_once = [i for i in range(NUM_PROMPTS) if not parses(prompts[i], all_at_once[i])]
print(f"REPRO invalid Python, groups of {SMALL_GROUP}: {len(broken_in_groups)} of {NUM_PROMPTS}", flush=True)
print(f"REPRO invalid Python, all {NUM_PROMPTS} at once: {len(broken_all_at_once)} of {NUM_PROMPTS} at {broken_all_at_once}", flush=True)
for i in broken_all_at_once[:3]:
    print(f"REPRO --- prompt {i}, groups of {SMALL_GROUP}:", flush=True)
    for line in in_groups[i].split("\n"):
        print("REPRO     |" + line, flush=True)
    print(f"REPRO --- prompt {i}, all at once:", flush=True)
    for line in all_at_once[i].split("\n"):
        print("REPRO     |" + line, flush=True)
```

</details>

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The cache-size control isolates pressure on the 112k-token KV cache, but the report does not establish that preemption occurs. In the reported vLLM revision, preemption frees a request's blocks and resets its computed-token count; tpu-inference removes unscheduled rows and re-adds resumed requests with replacement block IDs. That handoff is a testable hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. The reproducer uses vLLM `70ea9ae8f` and tpu-inference `v0.29.0`; Marin currently pins an older pair, and the failure occurs in standalone `LLM.generate`.

**Relevant code**
- [vLLM scheduler preemption](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/70ea9ae8f2601f06d820ee9d70e3afbdc52683b1/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1479-L1521) — frees blocks and resets progress
- [TPU persistent batch removal](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/persistent_batch_manager.py#L149-L201) — removes unscheduled rows
- [TPU resume path](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/persistent_batch_manager.py#L232-L334) — replaces block IDs and re-adds rows
- [TPU block-table construction](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/blob/v0.29.0/tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py#L2984-L3024) — maps batch rows to blocks
- [Marin TPU fork pins](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/config/external/vllm/tpu-forks.toml#L6-L16) — older serving pair

# Proposed Fix

1. Run the supplied v6e reproducer unchanged and capture scheduler preemption counts plus request IDs, computed-token counts, assigned block IDs, batch row IDs, and sampled token IDs around the first invalid completion. Repeat with the 32-request control and larger cache. This establishes whether the bad requests were preempted or merely admitted near the cache limit.
2. If bad tokens follow preemption, trace the request through scheduler reset, TPU batch removal/re-add, and block-table construction; assert that each resumed row uses its newly assigned blocks before decode. If no preemption occurs, inspect row-to-block mapping and sampled-token extraction for the last requests admitted in each wave.
3. Fix the identified path in vLLM or tpu-inference, add a regression that forces the same cache-pressure transition, and rerun the 256-prompt greedy repro on v6e and cache-limited v5p. Once it passes, refresh Marin's paired TPU fork pins and validate its serving path. The existing 32-request grouping is a temporary workload limit, not a correctness fix.

Done when all 256 completions parse in repeated runs at both 112k-token cache settings, with the regression passing on the affected fork.

issues.title: [tpu-inference] Completions corrupt when the KV cache fills (vLLM on TPU)

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

The benchmarks point in opposite directions in these single-training-run readouts. BFCL ×5 favors Muon-H (C150): 30.24% versus Adam (O150) at 24.55–24.72%. Overall Micro210 favors Adam: 41.92% versus 37.68% native equal-20, a difference of 12.46 assignment-weighted score-equivalents over 440 assignments. This is not 12 additional matched wins or a calibrated optimizer conclusion.

Both C150 and O150 start from the pretrained 2026.11.08.8 base, a BF16 import of pretraining step 157,000, not the 10/05 SFT model. Their Micro210 distances to 10/05 are not drops from their initializer. C150 also has slightly lower held-out pretraining loss; training loss is about the same. These readouts do not select Mochi's SFT optimizer by themselves.

## Description

The repo has two SFT paths:
- The `GrugRunConfig` path uses Muon-H, which matches pretraining.
- The native `SFTSpec` path defaults to Adam: cosine decay to 10%, gradient clip 1, no z-loss, no special-token update scaling, and assistant-only loss.

Mochi was pretrained with Muon-H. The 11-13 audit of two earlier SFT experiments, and advice in the marin-eng channel, both point to keeping the pretraining optimizer settings. This issue measures what the choice costs on Snowball.

Parent: issue 11535.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure whether switching SFT from Muon-H to Adam changes Snowball's tool use and retention of pretraining knowledge.

## Design

- Same pretrained Snowball base, 2026.11.08.8; same data and configured seed. Each arm trains 150 updates on 64 H100.
- C150: Muon-H.
- O150: Adam on all parameter groups, with the Adam grouping and clipping.
- One training run and one Micro210 evaluation per arm, so training-seed variability and evaluation repeat variability are not measured by this pair.

## Training and BFCL ×5 results

| | C150 (Muon-H) | O150 (Adam) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Final train loss | 0.4764 | 0.4755 |
| Held-out loss, mean of 4 pretraining sets | 0.8514 | 0.8553 |
| Held-out loss, mean of 11 SFT sets | 0.5098 | 0.5181 |
| BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks per run) | 186/615 = 30.24% | 151 known wins/615; 24.55–24.72% |
| Training cost (H100-h) | 144.97 | 166.10 |
| BFCL ×5 serving cost (H100-h) | 22.45 | 29.84 |

Lower loss is better. O150 is higher on all four pretraining sets. One set, identity data, decides the SFT mean: O150 is +0.116 higher there, while lower on eight of the eleven SFT sets. The retention readout of both arms cost 14.10 H100-h.

BFCL ×5 uses final-selected results, not first-attempt-only outcomes. One O150 selected trial has no verifier score, with an AddTestsDirError and a no-space symptom; the disk root cause is not established. Its outcome stays unknown. The range is a missing-outcome bound, not a confidence interval. O150 minus C150 is −5.69 to −5.53 percentage points on this benchmark.

## Micro210 results

Both evaluations completed on the current cw-us-east-02a harness: 16 global Harbor slots, one 8 H100 policy and an independent 8 H100 judge, 6 h policy/judge caps and a 7 h root cap. The same recipe has 200 supported tasks and 440 assignments, including 100 Pi assignments.

| Model | Native equal-20 | Available equal-20 | Pooled available | Scored / assigned | Excluded | Native score mass | Tasks vs 10/05 reference | BFCL /10 | Eval H100-h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C150 | 37.68% | 37.98% | 32.49% | 437 / 440 | 3 | 141.99 | -40.35 | 5* | 26.57 |
| O150 | 41.92% | 41.95% | 35.18% | 439 / 440 | 1 | 154.44 | -27.90 | 2 | 26.29 |

The reference is the completed 10/05 run 44627, native score mass 182.338705602. Since C150/O150 start from a different pretrained base, these are distances to that reference, not skill lost from their initializer. The missing reference for gains from 150 updates is the zero-update pretrained base, not 10/05.

Native equal-20 is recomputed from the 20 native per-source averages; their denominators include excluded assignments. Available-only means omit excluded outcomes. C150 has three unknowns: one BFCL and two TB2. O150 has one OT-TBLite unknown. Unknown is not a known failure or zero.

BFCL /10 is a separate ten-assignment Micro slice, not BFCL ×5. C150 has five known score units from nine scored assignments and one unknown, so its assigned-score bounds are 5–6/10; O150 has 2/10, fully scored. This small slice also favors C150, even though overall Micro210 favors O150.

The exact native mass difference is +12.455300305 score-equivalents for O150 versus C150. Allowing unknown outcomes in [0,1] gives [+9.455300305, +13.455300305]. These are missing-outcome bounds, not confidence intervals, matched individual task outcomes or measured evaluation noise. Fractional graders produce fractional score-equivalents, not integer additional wins. The same-configuration parent repeat's roughly five-task difference is descriptive, not a universal tie band.

Requested evaluation H100-hours are physical-attempt resource envelopes, not utilization or invoice totals. Native completion, produced suite-byte identity, assigned-UID membership and trace capture are separate proofs; exact source-file/task joins were not independently established for these rows. Nine broader import failures remain unresolved, not broad-suite green.

## Decision status and evidence

Micro210 is no longer pending for these two runs. BFCL ×5 and overall Micro210 disagree on the preferred optimizer. Further comparisons remain under discussion; repeat-evaluation packets are draft-only, with no new repeat result or submission implied here.

Reviewed detailed readout: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11537#issuecomment-6930443977

All-model comparison: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535#issuecomment-6956044426

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## Outcome

Marin Hero SFT (step 400407) showed modest discrimination on missense variants and ranked TSS-proximal pathogenic variants near chance against their matched controls. Adding “The following sequence is from a healthy individual:” gave no clear benefit on either subset. We are closing the investigation here. The deliverable is the branch-based experiment and its evidence.

## DNA likelihood

Each autosomal Mendelian train panel contained 30 matched groups, each with one pathogenic variant and nine common controls (10% positive). We scored reference and alternate 255-base sequences on both strands, using raw DNA with either an empty prefix or the healthy-individual prefix. The pathogenicity score was the mean reference-minus-alternate log likelihood across strands. Its direction was fixed before scoring.

| Panel | No prefix AUPRC | Healthy prefix AUPRC | Healthy minus no prefix (paired 95% interval) | Within-group wins, no prefix / healthy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 300 missense | 0.178 | 0.189 | +0.010 [−0.020, +0.070] | 61.1% / 60.7% |
| 300 TSS-proximal | 0.150 | 0.141 | −0.009 [−0.043, +0.007] | 50.0% / 49.3% |

Intervals use 2,000 matched-group bootstrap resamples. The promoter-like category includes non-exonic variants within 1 kb of a transcription start site. Each panel retained its original 100 variants. The expansion allowed overlapping windows and included 130 formerly reserved missense development variants. These are exploratory train results. The held-out test split was unused.

Historical missense likelihoods differed from the current serving configuration, so all 300 missense variants were rescored. The original TSS-proximal scores passed the sampled compatibility check. All 4,800 target likelihoods were accounted for and all 252 repeat checks matched exactly. The earlier missense pilot’s larger prefix gain cannot be attributed to sample size alone. [Full report and replay](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/expanded300-report.md) · [Metrics](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/expanded300-metrics.json) · [Per-variant scores](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/expanded300-variants.json)

## Direct classification

On the original 100 missense variants, FASTA/VCF prompts with scored A/B answers gave zero-shot / two-shot AUPRC of **0.110 / 0.101** with raw prompts and **0.157 / 0.118** with chat prefill. Chat prefill raised the probability assigned to the two answer letters, but the comparisons did not establish improved VEP discrimination. In zero-shot chat prefill, Hero preferred B in all 200 strand contexts. On easy non-DNA questions, it answered 24/24 contexts correctly across both letter assignments. The evidence supports sensitivity to the VEP prompt and label mapping. [Raw protocol and results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/pilot-v3-report.md) · [Chat comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/chat-pilot-report.md) · [Easy-question controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/easy-diagnostic-report.md) · [Cross-domain controls](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/cross-domain-report.md)

## Code and evidence at fixed revisions

- [Complete research directory, including scripts, prompts, tests, frozen inputs, scores and reports](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep) · [Chronological notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/notebook.md)
- [Panel selection, compatibility checks and aggregation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/expand_likelihood.py) · [Likelihood client](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/client.py) · [Bootstrap metrics](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/b163b766199ed76081e2cac6a9d56d22d5139c07/logbooks/11181-hero-vep/expanded300_metrics.py)
- [Marin experimental harness and prompt templates](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/59e1c63c153cb17446c60f7c6073df166f3ab490/experiments/evals/vep) · [Shared likelihood implementation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/59e1c63c153cb17446c60f7c6073df166f3ab490/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/likelihood.py) · [Likelihood tests](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/59e1c63c153cb17446c60f7c6073df166f3ab490/tests/evaluation/test_likelihood.py)

comments.body:
🤖 VEP-specific diagnostic complete. The effect is not limited to the literal B token:

- **B preferred 32/32 A/B contexts; D preferred 31/32 C/D contexts**, crossing both class assignments, both list orders, and real/shuffled DNA on four variants.
- Swapping class-to-letter mapping changes the semantic prediction in **31/32** matched pairs. Median absolute conditional pathogenic-probability change: **24.05 percentage points**.
- Reversing displayed option order changes that probability by median **7.30 points**; replacing A/B with C/D by **3.65**; shuffling DNA flanks by **2.10** (maximum shuffle effect 7.82). Last-listed option wins only 33/64.

This supports strong label/mapping dependence in this VEP prompt family, despite the successful easy-question controls. It does not establish useful biological sensitivity or a general training defect. The response instruction still says “A or B” / “C or D,” so last-mentioned label and alphabetic order remain confounded. More DNA examples alone would not remove this structural issue; a next control could reverse instruction mention order independently of list order. That run has not been launched.

All 261 HTTP requests succeeded in 133.40 seconds, with 68 generated tokens and 192 tokenization checks. Four repeats and four matching earlier pilot baselines reproduce exactly. comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Cross-domain investigation complete: **DNA is not necessary for label-mapping sensitivity**, but clear non-DNA questions do not reproduce the strong VEP effect.

- Four clear reviews: **64/64 correct** across mappings, option orders, instruction mention orders and short/structured context. These are four underlying reviews, not 64 independent examples.
- Two ambiguous reviews: semantic prediction flips in **6/16** matched mapping swaps; list order and instruction mention order each also flip 6/16. Ambiguous inputs are ungraded.
- Intuitive example: “Some features are good and some are bad. Overall I have mixed feelings about it.” With the same short prompt, B-then-A list order and A-or-B instruction, swapping only the class-to-letter assignment changes conditional P(positive) from **21.44% to 53.22%**. The model prefers B both times, so the semantic answer changes from negative to positive.
- VEP: B still preferred **32/32**, including “B or A” instructions. Mapping flips semantic predictions 16/16. A simple last-mentioned-letter explanation is insufficient.

This is consistent with answer priors having more influence under weak evidence, but does not prove the internal mechanism or a training defect. Added structured context exceeds VEP prompt length without breaking clear sentiment, so length alone is not a sufficient explanation either. The finding is ready to discuss as evaluation robustness with an intuitive example, retaining the ambiguity caveat; no Slack message was sent.

Ambiguous sentiment has no definitive answer key, so this is a robustness observation, not an accuracy failure. Weak-evidence fallback is plausible, but neither a training bug nor a need for retraining is established. These are small prompt diagnostics, not broad model-capability estimates.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

Integrate the original 5,200-question [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) through **TaskCompendium** in PR #10984. Six biological subtasks, one answer per question, no tools or retrieval. The PR targets current `main` and reuses the native evaluation pipeline.

| Topic | Agreed approach |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Pinned `HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa` BCQ and MCQ data. All 5,200 rows match the author release on evaluation fields. Preserve DNA text and option order; exclude Carbon’s modified tasks and subsets. |
| Reporting | Foreground six biological subtask scores. Average BCQ/MCQ equally within each subtask, then average subtasks equally. Retain format summaries, all 12 cells, denominators, and unweighted correct counts. No chance correction. |
| Prompt | Fetch the pinned public runner’s fixed optimized prompt externally, as data. Optimization already happened offline; no new prompt search or bundled prompt. |
| Generation | Temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, seed 42, one response, and a shared 16,384-token total output cap including reasoning and answer. Verify model-specific thinking controls. Full prompts and the entire output allowance must fit. |
| Implementation | Reuse native acquisition, Parquet reading, conversion, source-grader packaging, final-only response selection, retries, and weighted reduction. Keep only GenomeQA’s parser, source checks, weights, and groups specific to this benchmark. |
| Grading | Grade final content only. Ambiguous, invalid, missing, and length-truncated answers score zero; transport failures remain ungraded. Retain the agreed parser rather than adding natural-language recovery worth only 0.0167 points on Maverick. |
| Asset handling | Dataset/prompt reuse terms remain unspecified. Tests are synthetic; questions and responses remain in controlled storage. Public reports contain aggregates. External fetching does not resolve use terms. |

### Why

A model can describe a splice site in words. Can it also recognize one when given a DNA sequence? GenomeQA lets us test that distinction with sequence-based questions about regulatory elements, splice sites, species, histone marks, transcription-factor binding sites, and motifs. The six subtask scores show where a model can select the correct biological label from the sequence and where it struggles. That gives us a way to compare checkpoints and track which sequence tasks improve as training changes.

### Validation

All six native runs are complete: **5,200/5,200 graded per run**. They use the same questions, prompt, sampling, and total output cap. GPT-OSS reasons at both settings: low/medium is not off/on. These are single-seed comparisons, not claims of statistical superiority.

| Biological subtask | Gemma off | Gemma on | Qwen off | Qwen on | GPT-OSS low | GPT-OSS medium |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 38.60% | 36.30% | 47.20% | 50.40% | 48.90% | 50.00% |
| Splice sites | 37.30% | 23.40% | 29.70% | 32.00% | 37.70% | 35.00% |
| Species classification | 47.10% | 34.90% | 50.00% | 50.20% | 49.90% | 49.40% |
| Histone marks | 40.70% | 31.70% | 40.40% | 38.80% | 39.70% | 40.20% |
| TF binding sites | 41.80% | 39.40% | 41.80% | 42.60% | 46.30% | 45.70% |
| Motifs | 59.00% | 69.00% | 57.00% | 59.50% | 60.00% | 60.00% |
| **Overall macro** | **44.08%** | **39.12%** | **44.35%** | **45.58%** | **47.08%** | **46.72%** |
| Truncations / 5,200 | 12 | 1341 | 318 | 393 | 34 | 42 |

Gemma thinking falls **4.97 points**, with 25.79% truncation; Qwen thinking rises **1.23 points**; GPT-OSS medium falls **0.37 points**. All six have zero parsing failures and separately classified refusals. Truncations remain zero-scored in the full denominator. They materially limit interpretation of Gemma’s thinking-on result.

- **Paper comparison.** Maverick scored 50.60% on all 5,200 questions versus 49.07% derived from the paper’s binary-choice and multiple-choice tables.
- **Replay.** We verified the prompts, generation settings, and weights for 31,200 saved responses. Replaying them through the corrected grader at `b706dbdc87` reproduced every native extracted answer and metric. All 26 grader/importer tests passed.
- **Blinded spot check.** A single Codex reviewer labeled 24 saved responses before seeing the references or grades. All 24 agreed on extraction and score: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six truncated. The sample included one truncation per run.

### Cost

**The six native runs consumed 30.03 H100-hours** including serving and recovery. Worker time sums the durations of started worker attempts. Elapsed time spans the first worker start to the last worker stop, including recovery gaps and excluding the initial queue wait.

| Scope | H100s per worker | Worker time (min) | Elapsed (min) | H100-hours |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Gemma off and on, including recovery | 2 | 399 | 5,310 | 13.29 |
| Qwen off | 4 | 91 | 91 | 6.04 |
| Qwen on | 4 | 118 | 118 | 7.86 |
| GPT-OSS low | 1 | 95 | 226 | 1.58 |
| GPT-OSS medium | 1 | 76 | 76 | 1.26 |

<details>
<summary>Model pins, usage, replay evidence, and recovery details</summary>

Current-main validation (2026-11-17, `5e07ba7498`): **23 focused tests and lint pass; all applicable CI checks are green**. The PR reuses main’s `final_only` implementation; its custom shared-code addition is removed. All six advisory lanes completed; fixes reuse the existing Parquet reader and centralize repeated constants. The compact grader and source-row dictionaries were retained because splitting this linear grading operation or wrapping boundary rows would add little value.

The current-main audit is complete: **all 31,200 saved answers across six runs match**, with zero source-row, prompt, generation-setting, extracted-answer, metric, or weight differences. All expected cell populations and latest graded attempts were verified. The upstream `final_only` change alters none of these results; no saved message combines a refusal field with nonempty content. Follow-up constant cleanup is semantically identical, and the shared Parquet reader preserves all 5,200 source hashes. The CPU-only audit succeeded within its one-hour cap, with **zero new model calls**.

Private EvalDash ingestion reproduces all six macros, all six subtask and twelve cell metrics, and full 5,200-item coverage. The macro remains continuous, with weighted uncertainty and no fabricated integer correct count. **A shared reporting gap remains:** `coverage.n_unanswered` is not populated by the native reader, although the `unanswered` and truncation metrics are correct. No public records were ingested; this verifies backend reduction and measurement projection, not browser rendering.

Historical paper comparison: Maverick’s complete 5,200-question run scored **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ table. Replaying it through TaskCompendium reproduced every per-item metric and all 120 grouped metrics with identical prompts. A separate two-question live native smoke also passed.

Review fixes in `b706dbdc87` reject `B1` and `B or (C)`, identify renamed pinned input files by digest, and independently test wrong answers and cell populations. All 26 grader/importer tests and changed-file lint passed. CI passed. A CPU-only replay of all 31,200 native final answers on the corrected grader found zero changes to extracted answers or metrics. Rechecking all 5,200 historical Maverick responses changed one histone MCQ from unparseable to a valid wrong answer (B, gold A). Its parse failures fall from six to five and the macro stays 50.60%.

**Blinded spot check at `b706dbdc87`.** A single Codex reviewer inspected 24 saved responses, four per run and 12 per format, and recorded the final choices before seeing the answer key or grader verdicts. All 24 extracted answers and grades agreed: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six length-truncated. Four truncations had empty final content and two had partial text; all six scored zero. Sampling deliberately included one truncation per run. This checks grading against the pinned answers, without estimating a population error rate or assessing the biological validity of the answer key.

Unlike the [merged SimpleQA Verified example (#11393)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11393)’s 2,048/16,384 off/on allowances, these comparisons keep the output cap equal to avoid changing both thinking and budget.

All native inference used runtime `fe813e34c2a0d047f10a1604a12da35f162031cd`. Gemma: `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` at `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`, two H100s. Qwen: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`, four H100s (TP2 × DP2). GPT-OSS: `openai/gpt-oss-20b` at `6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee`, one H100. Compilation and CUDA graphs remained enabled. Template checks and saved request options verify the selected thinking/effort controls. Other settings retain checkpoint/server defaults; these are fixed GenomeQA-protocol runs, not each model’s full recommended sampling recipe.

| Run | Input tokens | Output tokens | BCQ macro | MCQ macro |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gemma-off | 7,298,523 | 1,436,334 | 54.43% | 33.73% |
| gemma-on | 7,288,123 | 47,058,415 | 49.47% | 28.77% |
| qwen-off | 7,654,474 | 13,909,197 | 51.87% | 36.83% |
| qwen-on | 7,644,074 | 28,897,134 | 54.03% | 37.13% |
| gptoss-low | 7,812,272 | 8,041,128 | 53.77% | 40.40% |
| gptoss-medium | 7,812,272 | 8,005,514 | 54.73% | 38.70% |

Usage covers final graded attempts only; output includes reasoning and final answers without a separately measured split. Qwen thinking uses 2.08× output tokens; GPT-OSS medium uses 0.44% fewer than low. Failed-attempt usage is not included.

This is historical worker runtime, including serving overhead, not billing or a sum of authorization caps. Queue-only attempts have no start timestamp and contribute zero. Gemma’s paired/recovery workers span both modes, so their time is not falsely split. GPT-OSS low includes the preempted worker and successful recovery; its capacity-blocked recovery obtained no GPU. All inference workers are stopped. The subsequent audit is CPU-only and makes no model calls.

Native retries retained successful answers. Gemma’s final one-question recovery preserved all 5,199 prior responses; GPT-OSS low recovery preserved all 5,058. Qwen on recovered 28 first-pass infrastructure failures; GPT-OSS medium recovered 126 across two further native passes. Successful grades were not resampled. Earlier queue, connection, and preemption failures are operational history, not additional scored model failures.

Private audit evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/audit-merged-main-20261117/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Faudit-merged-main-20261117%2F). Includes per-item hashes, aggregate audits, ingestion projections, worker timestamps, and the prior detailed issue record.

Native result roots: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/gemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fgemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112%2F), and `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/cohort-fe813e34-20261116/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fcohort-fe813e34-20261116%2F). Original questions/responses remain controlled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered and rationale</summary>

| Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale and tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use pinned HF `binary` and `mcq` data. | Load the authors’ twelve JSONL files directly; rebuild questions from upstream biological databases. | All 5,200 HF rows matched the author release on evaluation fields. HF fits existing loading components. Direct JSONL would also be valid but offers little functional benefit after the equivalence check. Rebuilding could change sampling, filtering, and questions. Metadata equivalence remains unchecked. |
| Evaluate the original full benchmark. | Carbon’s modified MCQ dataset; 600-row or organism-specific subsets. | Preserve the original six task families and both formats. Carbon changes the taxonomy task; subsets change coverage. Neither should silently replace the original benchmark. |
| Use TaskCompendium’s existing evaluation components. | Retain the first vendored Evalchemy adapter; adopt the authors’ runner or Carbon’s Inspect evaluator. | The new-evaluation architecture supersedes the original Evalchemy decision. Reuse acquisition, conversion, grader packaging, and protocol/group metadata; preserve the benchmark independently of its original runner. The migration has since merged; reuse its native corpus path without adding public launcher registration. |
| Reuse the grader’s existing stop-reason channel. | Add a new transport for complete provider metadata. | Keep truncation handling without expanding the runtime. The `content_filter` stop reason is classified as refusal. Missing final content scores zero without reasoning fallback; original provider messages remain in the raw archive. Reuse main’s `final_only` selector without a GenomeQA-specific refusal override. |
| Retain existing runtime failure, retry, and coverage behavior. | Add opt-in empty-response and strict-completeness policies. | These concerns apply across benchmarks and do not justify shared runtime changes for GenomeQA. Remove the proposed policies and their tests; inspect coverage before reporting complete results. |
| Report raw accuracy. | Normalize accuracy relative to chance. | Ordinary correct/total accuracy is interpretable and preserves the paper’s metric. BCQ and MCQ have different chance levels; retain their separate results rather than changing the metric to compensate. |
| Weight the six subtasks equally and the two formats equally. | Pool all 5,200 questions into micro-accuracy. | Pooling would give motifs five times less weight than each other family because it has fewer questions. Equal weighting treats each biological capability as one component. |
| Foreground six subtask scores and their overall mean. | Foreground BCQ/MCQ summaries; show only a combined score; show only the two format scores. | The research priority is understanding biological strengths and weaknesses. First average BCQ/MCQ within each subtask, then average subtasks. Reversing that order gives the same overall number with equal weights; the decision concerns presentation. Keep all 12 cells and both format summaries as secondary diagnostics. |
| Retain the authors’ fixed optimized system prompt and user layout. | Minimal generic prompting; Carbon’s Inspect multiple-choice prompt; repeat prompt optimization. | Use an established prompt for the original questions and avoid introducing an additional variable. Optimization already occurred offline; the fixed prompt is in the public runner. The resulting scores measure capability with supplied biological guidance. Generic prompting could support a separate ablation, but is not part of this integration. |
| Reuse shared final-response cleanup, then a small GenomeQA-specific letter parser. | Copy the authors’ complete parser; use the shared HLE/GPQA extractors unchanged; introduce a separate extraction implementation. | Synthetic checks showed that existing first/last-letter extractors can select incidental analysis or trailing letters. The custom parser handles final-section isolation, explicit declarations, conflicts, and valid options; shared response representation and thinking cleanup are reused. This deliberately adapts the author parser rather than claiming exact extraction parity. |
| Accept an unambiguous explicit `Answer: X` when the heading is missing. | Require the exact `### Answer` heading for every response. | A clearly stated answer should not be marked wrong solely for omitting a heading. Conflicting markers and missing answers still require focused validation; do not recover answers from hidden reasoning. |
| Apply one shared total generated-token cap across models. | Model-specific recommended caps; leave limits to provider defaults as the author runner does; cap only the answer text. | Bound generation consistently across a large question set. Include reasoning, visible analysis, and final answer. This equalizes nominal token allowance, not compute, latency, or tokenizer efficiency. Provider semantics must be verified. |
| Start with 16,384 generated tokens per question. | Start with 32,768 tokens. | Limit cost and latency over 5,200 questions. The tighter cap may increase truncations; report them by model and subtask. This is an initial evaluation choice, not a budget validated by the GenomeQA paper. |
| Enable thinking where supported and pin effort per model configuration. | Always use provider-recommended mode, including thinking off; use the same named effort for every model; use maximum effort everywhere. | Follow the GPQA/MMLU-Pro thinking-on pattern in the current policy. Identical effort labels do not imply equivalent reasoning across providers, and maximum effort may exhaust the total budget before an answer. The validation pairs use Gemma/Qwen thinking off/on and GPT-OSS low/medium effort; GPT-OSS has no true thinking-off setting. |
| Request temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.95. | Provider-recommended sampling; temperature 0 as in MMLU-Pro; Carbon-X’s 0.6/0.95/top-k 20 settings. | Retain the settings requested by the released GenomeQA runner alongside its prompt. Marin’s reasoning-Q&A precedents are mixed: GPQA uses 0.7, MMLU-Pro uses greedy generation. This is a GenomeQA protocol choice, not a universal Marin rule. Document unsupported provider parameters and deviations. |
| First-pass paper comparison: Llama-4 Maverick on the complete TF-motif MCQ cell (100 questions). | No paper-model check; a full 5,200-question run; a 600-question stratified sample across all 12 cells; the complete enhancer/promoter MCQ cell (500 questions). | A complete cell permits direct comparison with an entry in the paper’s table; a cross-cell sample would use different question coverage. Motif MCQ is the smallest complete cell, and Maverick avoids reasoning-effort ambiguity. This was the initial scope. The later authorized full-benchmark validation is recorded above; retain the small check as historical evidence and retire its temporary integration code. |
| Proceed with independently written integration code and runtime HF loading; do not redistribute benchmark questions. | Wait indefinitely for author permission; vendor the upstream code, prompt, and dataset together. | An author response is not a prerequisite for adapter development. Keep the dataset license explicitly unspecified, use synthetic test fixtures, and keep question text out of public artifacts. Runtime fetching reduces redistribution but does not resolve missing dataset-use terms. |
| Keep the pinned runner prompt external and load its string without executing upstream code. | Bundle the runner prompt; use the CC BY paper’s Figure 8 prompt; write a new prompt. | Figure 8 is shorter than the runner: it omits the explicit binary-letter instruction and some reasoning guidance. Using it would change the agreed protocol. External loading preserves that protocol without bundling the prompt; it does not establish a license for the external asset. |

Batch submission was also considered: no Maverick batch endpoint was listed during validation. The run used concurrent synchronous requests, following the existing evaluation pattern, rather than adding batch infrastructure. Carbon’s Inspect evaluator uses a modified MCQ dataset and different prompting; its scores are not a parity target for this integration.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Pinned assets, parser details, and historical parity</summary>

Data: [HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943), revision `e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943`; only `binary/train-00000-of-00001.parquet` and `mcq/train-00000-of-00001.parquet`. The `train` split is used for evaluation. Evaluation fields match the author release; metadata equivalence was not checked.

Binary SHA-256: `0ef4c3d33541980e3fded9a5b23a952296ce3c51cb0415b42c0299a61c21938a`; MCQ: `c1cbb51449eb8a5241890337c88dc1bc0a58974b8eb4cb8bc49f310b12faeb75`.

Prompt: authors’ [run.py](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py), revision `7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d`. Parse the literal without executing upstream code. Prompt-development-set disjointness has not been established. The paper’s CC BY Figure 8 differs from the runner; it is not substituted. Code/data availability statements do not establish reuse terms for the assembled dataset or runner prompt.

For each subtask, average its BCQ and MCQ accuracies; overall is the mean of those six values. Reversing the two equal-weight averaging steps gives the same result. `genomeqa_macro` uses weight 5 for the 100-question motif cells and 1 for each 500-question cell; ordinary accuracy remains unweighted. Format macros follow the authors’ [aggregation](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/collect_res.py).

Parsing selects final content, strips completed thinking blocks, isolates the last `### Answer` section, and accepts one valid option. Without a heading, an unambiguous explicit `Answer: X` is accepted. Conflicting options, incomplete thinking blocks, missing answers, and `length` completions score zero. `content_filter` is separately classified as refusal. Main’s shared `final_only` selector returns content without reasoning fallback or a benchmark-specific refusal-field override. The saved Gemma thinking-on run contains 1,321 empty final-content responses with nonempty reasoning; they remain zero-scored rather than extracting an answer from reasoning. Raw messages remain archived.

Maverick (2026-11-06, historical Evalchemy path): macro 50.60%, BCQ 57.43%, MCQ 43.77%, unweighted 47.46% (2,468/5,200); paper-derived macro 49.07%. Six parse failures, no truncations or separately classified refusals. Four failures were splice-site MCQ, one histone MCQ, one TFBS MCQ. Natural-language declarations such as “The answer is X” would recover one additional correct answer: macro 50.6167%. Those counterfactual scores were not adopted. Reported API cost was $3.08, conservative accounting bound $3.93, excluding CPU hosting and connectivity pilot.

The first complete motif-MCQ cell scored 64/100 versus the paper’s 65/100; its temporary integration code was retired after the full run. Historical full-response replay matched all 5,200 requests, metrics, and extracted answers, including the six parse failures. The two-question native smoke used 1,982 input and 348 output tokens ($0.0010417 API cost); it validates execution, not performance. Its provider request included seed/thinking kwargs absent from the historical run, without proving provider enforcement.

Carbon-X uses a modified MCQ taxonomy task, different prompting, and different generation defaults. Its Inspect evaluator is not a parity target. Marin’s [evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) has mixed sampling precedents—GPQA 0.7, MMLU-Pro greedy—not a universal provider-default rule. Migration #10957 superseded the original vendored-Evalchemy design; the final adapter uses native TaskCompendium and main’s shared response selector. No changes to other issues or PRs are required.

</details>

### Remaining scope

- #10984 has green CI and squash auto-merge enabled; GitHub’s required approving review is still pending.
- Before public reporting: resolve sample-access controls and the shared unanswered-count metadata gap, then validate the browser presentation of six subtask scores. Additional scalar metrics alone do not create six dashboard columns.
- Official-policy admission remains a separate research decision. No further inference is required for this adapter’s validation.
