issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
# [evals] Evaluate ScienceAgentBench Verified for ID-policy inclusion

## Summary

Implement [ScienceAgentBench Verified](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench)
as TaskSpecs and collect evidence for inclusion in
[Marin's ID evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197).
The proposed outcome is a reproducible implementation, complete runs on selected
cohort models through the official EvalDash path, and a documented admission
recommendation. Policy inclusion remains a separate decision.

Execution order: implement and validate all 102 reference solutions, run the
204-trial Qwen panel through the official evaluation path, review its outcomes,
run the remaining cohort, and present the admission recommendation.

Initial source inspection supports pursuing Verified, but the artifact audit,
agentic evaluation integration, and execution evidence are outstanding. Harbor's
existing adapter supplies historical reference material; it does not establish
Verified compatibility.

The benchmark tests scientific Python programming with supplied data across
bioinformatics, computational chemistry, geographical information science, and
psychology/cognitive science. The inclusion case will document the measured
capabilities, trustworthy grading, cohort results, reproducibility, and
operational cost. An incremental-coverage or overlap assessment against existing
ID evaluations is outside this issue's scope.

## Evidence standard

[SimpleQA Verified PR #11393](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11393)
provides an example of the evidence package for a new evaluation:

- What capability is measured and why it belongs in the evaluation set.
- Pinned data, implementation, prompts, models, and explicit protocol deviations.
- Complete baseline runs with EvalDash links and comparison to published results.
- Grading audits, failures, and limitations.
- End-to-end runtime, accelerator use, and judge cost.

Registration, full execution, verified dashboard ingestion, and policy admission
are separate milestones. An EvalDash entry alone does not establish policy approval.

## Source findings

### Verified modifies the original task population

It is a modification of the same 102 task IDs, not a smaller subset.

<details>
<summary>Annotation comparison: 41 of 102 rows changed</summary>

A direct comparison of the public annotation files at Hugging Face revision
`9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7` found:

| Comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original annotation rows | 102 |
| Verified annotation rows | 102 |
| Added or removed instance IDs | None |
| Rows with at least one changed field | 41 |
| Task instruction changes | 9 tasks |
| Domain knowledge changes | 4 tasks |
| Dataset preview changes | 18 tasks |
| Source file/path changes | 15 tasks |

Field counts overlap. The comparison normalized null and empty values to the same
empty string and compared other values as strings; it is an annotation comparison,
not an audit of the underlying datasets or grading artifacts.

Changed task instructions: 12, 26, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35, 67, 92.
Changed domain knowledge: 5, 9, 79, 80.

Sources:
[original CSV](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/ScienceAgentBench.csv),
[Verified annotations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/data/verified-00000-of-00001.parquet).

</details>

Upstream describes Verified as a release to reduce false negatives and requires
both the Verified annotations and `benchmark_verified.zip`. The November 17
artifact audit below establishes its inventory and selected grading structure.
The historical artifact link returns HTTP 404, so exact legacy-to-Verified
evaluator, reference-output, input-data, and dependency changes remain unresolved.
Do not describe this as a grading-only fix.

### Verified artifact audit — November 17, 2026

The archive linked by the current upstream README is 1,769,478,786 bytes;
streamed SHA-256: `46e715d3b2196d459d2dff52aa487f506a95ec44b44262e82208d086ea879610`.
Its 955 entries total 4,071,815,117 uncompressed bytes. Ranged reads retrieved
only the small program/rubric files for static inspection; restricted source
files remain private and were not committed or redistributed.

- All 102 annotation-referenced evaluators and reference programs are present.
  There are 110 Python files in the evaluator directory; only the annotation
  mapping defines the evaluation population.
- The selected evaluators comprise 38 deterministic and 64 visual tasks.
  Sixty-three visual tasks make one figure comparison. Task 63 makes two;
  each figure's mean judge score must be at least 60 for the task to pass.
  The single-figure visual evaluators also use the threshold of 60.
- Task 63 requires both figure outputs. Capturing only each annotation's
  `output_fname` would omit its second output; capture the required output set
  from clean replay before grading.
- Task 22 calls `pandas.read_pickle` on candidate output. Its deserialization
  requires an additional isolation boundary or an explicitly validated safe
  representation; moving program execution out of the grader is insufficient
  to isolate that task's untrusted output.
- The largest dataset directory is approximately 863.28 MiB. This is input-data
  size, not prepared image size or peak disk usage, and does not yet prove that
  every task fits the selected 10 GiB allocation.

This audit is static evidence. Reference execution, full data/dependency
validation, and the original-versus-Verified artifact comparison remain pending.

### Harbor generation is unpinned and targets the legacy split

There are two separate issues:

1. **Reproducibility:** the generator calls `load_dataset` without a revision.
   Regenerating tasks can therefore change when upstream changes. This is a
   reproducibility defect for a canonical evaluation, though it does not prove
   already-generated, separately pinned Harbor tasks are mutable.
2. **Current loader compatibility:** the generator loads the default configuration
   and indexes `['validation']`. The current HF default configuration exposes
   `verified`; the legacy `validation` split lives in a separate configuration
   named `validation`. The existing code is therefore expected to fail on a fresh
   current load with a missing-split error. This is a source-level finding; the
   adapter has not been executed here.

For Verified, explicitly select `split="verified"` and a full HF revision, paired
with the matching artifact checksum. Reproducing the legacy benchmark requires an
explicit legacy config/revision and its matching artifacts. Neither choice should
silently replace the other.

Sources: [adapter.py](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/adapter.py),
[run_adapter.py](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/run_adapter.py),
[HF configuration](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/README.md).

## Existing implementation and evidence

- [Harbor PR #630](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/630) merged on
  April 18, 2026. [Upstream](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench)
  announced Verified on April 30, 2026.
- Harbor documents 102 legacy tasks: 38 deterministic and 64 visual-judge tasks.
  Recheck this classification against Verified artifacts.
- Historical parity used Claude Code 2.1.63 with Claude Haiku 4.5, five runs per
  framework: Harbor 31.76% ± 1.18 percentage points SEM; patched upstream harness
  33.72% ± 0.91. The upstream harness had output-path and dependency fixes. These
  are legacy parity results, not Verified or Marin results.
- The current README reports 95/102 CPU oracle passes, with failures attributed
  to resource needs and stochastic variation. The PR description reports 100/102;
  that discrepancy needs reconciliation rather than selecting the stronger claim.
- Earlier Marin research in [issue #9160](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9160)
  prioritized a deterministic bioinformatics subset for readiness checks. That is
  a different scope from full Verified evaluation.

Historical evidence: [README](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/README.md),
[parity record](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/parity_experiment.json).

## Grading concerns to resolve

The [Harbor verifier](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/template/tests/test.sh)
turns missing or unreadable evaluation results into zero rewards. Infrastructure
failures must remain distinguishable from valid model failures.

The verifier also copies gold references into the execution filesystem before
rerunning submitted code. Although they are hidden during agent generation, they
are accessible during that later execution. Separate submitted-program execution
from grading, including reference files and judge credentials. This is a static
boundary finding, not an observed exploitation result.

The upstream visual judge uses GPT-4o-2024-05-13, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, 1,000 output
tokens, and three completions per request (`n=3`). Missing score markers become
zero in both inspected upstream and Harbor implementations. Decide and document
whether to preserve that behavior for parity or use an explicitly versioned
failure-aware protocol. Do not silently change grading semantics. Extract, pin, and test Verified's
exact task-success calculation, including aggregation across multiple figures
and mixed checks, pass thresholds, and missing candidate-output rules. Keep
malformed judge responses separate from valid negative judgments.

Sources: [upstream judge](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/gpt4_visual_judge.py),
[Harbor judge](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/llm_visual_judge.py).

## TaskSpec route: recommendation and remaining integration work

Recommendation: implement Verified as canonical TaskSpecs in TaskCompendium and
use Marin's shared rollout/evaluation infrastructure. Treat the Harbor adapter as
a reference and historical comparison, rather than the new implementation home.
This is a design recommendation, not a claim that interactive SAB already runs
through the curated evaluation launcher.

### Rationale

TaskCompendium represents the task, environment requirements, submitted files, and
private grader resources. Using that contract lets the implementation share
Marin's rollout and evaluation infrastructure while retaining upstream provenance.

Implementation compatibility and externally reportable benchmark validity require
separate evidence. Compare the new route against upstream Verified, document
protocol differences, and resolve the reporting criteria before claiming parity.

For SAB, directly convert the frozen source tasks. TaskForge generation and RL
quality filtering would change the benchmark population and are not required.
The evaluation corpus path preserves every source row and rejects missing,
rejected, or rewritten rows during publication.

### Task format versus agent harness

TaskSpec defines the problem, input environment, submission, and grader. It does
not select Pi or any other agent. RolloutEngine orchestrates execution, and
Shellbox supplies execution machines. The built-in `ShellHarness` runs Marin's
own tool loop; it is not Pi and should not be called a distinct "TaskSpec agent."

Policy [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197), rechecked
November 16, 2026, specifies Harbor / Pi for BixBench and pins Pi 0.87.0. Pi 0.87.0 is selected for consistency with the existing policy. TaskSpec and Pi
are complementary choices, but their integration must be proved: RolloutEngine
has an external `AgentHarness` interface, which alone does not establish a ready
Pi connector or canonical EvalDash integration. No Pi connector was found in the
local RolloutEngine/TaskCompendium runtime search. The desired design is TaskSpec
benchmark ownership with one agreed agent; any required shared runtime changes
remain separate from benchmark conversion.

### Proposed mapping

| SAB component | TaskSpec / runtime responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned task instruction and supplied knowledge | TaskSpec context, with explicit knowledge protocol |
| Input datasets and scientific software | Actor environment with digest-pinned image and private artifact provisioning |
| Interactive coding and debugging | RolloutEngine agent harness and native Shellbox execution |
| Submitted Python program | Explicit declared file submission; keep program identity and evidence |
| Clean replay of submitted program | Reference-free execution stage with its own limits and pinned dependencies |
| Deterministic checks and visual judging | Separate grading stage using upstream Verified assets; judge credentials only here |
| Population, repeats, sampling, metrics | EvaluationProtocol and immutable corpus |
| Raw attempts and dashboard presentation | Shared evaluation runner, FineStore archive, and verified EvalDash ingestion |

TaskSpec already represents file/workspace submissions, separate actor and grader
environments, private verifier resources, and scripted graders. That is a good
semantic fit. However, simply putting the replayed program into a fresh grader
machine alongside gold files would recreate the reference-access problem. The
reference-free replay and subsequent grading boundary still require explicit
implementation and validation. TaskSpec has no built-in ordered-stage contract.

### Current integration gaps

As of November 17, [PR #11576](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11576)
is open and introduces an `add-eval` skill and guide for non-agentic curated
evaluations. Its [guide at the inspected revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2dd5aa45254641ef3c2977afa49cdc2afa34c1e6/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md)
explicitly directs agentic benchmarks to Harbor. It does not supply a ready
TaskSpec/Pi evaluation route. Reuse the shared migration's supported interfaces
as they become available; keep benchmark conversion separate from shared runtime
work and avoid a benchmark-specific replacement runner. TaskSpec remains the
selected benchmark contract. Any interim Harbor execution must be identified
separately and must not be presented as completion of the TaskSpec integration.

1. **Interactive evaluation runner.** Both revision `246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7` and main inspected on
   November 13, 2026 hard-code `ExactChatHarness` in
   `marin.rollouts.evaluation._score_generation`. That harness accepts a
   conversational answer and rejects tools. The broader RolloutEngine supports
   agent execution, but the curated evaluation path needs an appropriate supported
   harness selection and file-submission integration. Merely registering a TaskSpec
   will not enable a terminal agent.
2. **Native environments.** TaskSpec supports digest-pinned images and, on the
   local Shellbox backend, hash-pinned Python package locks. Prebuilt images are
   the proposed route for SAB's scientific system dependencies and accelerator
   needs. Unresolved Docker build recipes cannot execute through the documented
   task adapters. Confirm backend GPU, RAM, disk, and network support per task.
3. **File transfer.** The documented submission transfer is limited to 1,024 files
   and 16 MiB total. Transferring the submitted program may fit easily, but output
   artifacts and any replay-to-grader handoff require measured size checks.
4. **Visual judge.** Validate image payloads, three-completion behavior, immutable
   judge identity, and secret isolation through the supported judge transport.
   Existing text-judge support alone does not establish visual-judge parity.
5. **Reporting.** Prove canonical launcher/archive/EvalDash behavior with an actual
   agentic task. Successful generic RolloutEngine execution is not sufficient.
   Retain an upstream Verified comparison for scientific validity; do not assume
   TaskSpec scores automatically satisfy external reporting policy.

Implementation checks must exercise both deterministic and visual grading,
including actor execution, clean replay, archived evidence, and EvalDash display.
These checks are not a separate two-task model pilot: the first model panel is
the full 204-trial Qwen run, after full population preparation and reference
validation. Do not substitute a
single-response code-generation protocol solely to fit the current runner; that
would be a distinct evaluation from the proposed interactive agent protocol.

Upstream's [metric calculation](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/calculate_metrics.py)
selects the best trajectory separately for each task, using success, program
validity, CodeBERTScore, then cost to break ties. Its reported cost averages the
selected trajectories. Our operational cost report must count all attempts,
retries, and judge calls, including trajectories that were not selected.

The official [inference instructions](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/README.md#direct-prompting-and-self-debug)
expose `--use_knowledge` as an option, and the
[native agent](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/agent.py)
defaults to `use_knowledge=False`. Including the supplied knowledge is a supported
benchmark variant. Here the repository agent means the authors' direct-prompting
and self-debug implementation, not a uniquely canonical agent protocol.
[Paper Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S4.T3) reports both with-knowledge
and without-knowledge results for direct prompting, OpenHands CodeAct, and
self-debug. The code default does not establish a preferred paper setting.
These paper results predate Verified. Comparisons must match the knowledge
setting as well as the benchmark version. The selected plan is two separately
reported conditions for each of the three models: six model-condition cells.
One trial per task per model per knowledge condition is selected: 612 planned
solver trials, excluding validation and separately accounted infrastructure
retries. This protocol decision does not authorize execution or spending.

### Image preparation strategy (selected)

Selected: prepare and validate images before scored trials, then use immutable image digests
across models, knowledge conditions, and retries. This is compatible with the
TaskSpec image route, which requires resolving Docker build recipes before
execution. A fresh container per trial still preserves isolation; reusing an image
must never reuse a model's modified workspace.

BixBench and BFCL campaign configurations explicitly require preparing selected
task images with Pi before launch. Policy #10197 describes DS-1000 images built
from pinned Dockerfiles; that statement does not establish whether builds occur
for every trial or whether caches are reused. There is no single image-preparation
procedure established here for every policy evaluation.

SAB's Harbor adapter provides Dockerfile recipes with scientific dependencies and
task input data. Those recipes can be built ahead of time. For the proposed
Verified implementation, keep Pi in the actor environment only, keep clean replay
free of gold references and judge credentials, and expose private grading assets
only to the grading stage. Preserve the upstream dependency semantics when
preparing each stage; preinstallation must not silently change the benchmark.

Preparation adds up-front build/validation work and registry storage, but avoids
repeating dependency installation during scored trials and lets every comparison
use the same image bytes. Large images still need pulling and backend startup;
prepared images do not guarantee zero setup time. Any images containing restricted
SAB data must remain private, and a changed dependency requires a newly versioned
image and corresponding validation.

The image-build deadline governs preparation work, separately from the six-minute
agent setup, 60-minute solving, and 30-minute verifier budgets. Match BixBench's
preparation behavior without a benchmark-specific timeout override. Verify and
record the effective timeout in the preparation path before building; no explicit
campaign override does not imply unlimited build time. Harbor's 30-minute SAB
template allowance is comparison evidence, not the selected preparation limit.

### Timing evidence for the protocol decision

The [paper introduction](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S1) says agents can
usually produce a meaningful program draft within 10 minutes. This is a broad
observation, not a reported end-to-end runtime distribution or agent deadline.
[Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#A1) says task collection was
restricted to programs that complete within 10 minutes; this concerns program
execution, not the entire agent session.

In upstream code at `c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d`,
[agent.py](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/agent.py)
allows up to 10 self-debug iterations and 900 seconds per program execution.
[run_eval.py](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/run_eval.py)
also uses 900 seconds for submitted-program execution. The
[Docker evaluation CLI](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/evaluation/harness/run_evaluation.py)
defaults to 1,800 seconds for tests per instance. These are distinct limits.
The selected Pi agent budget is 60 minutes per task, matching the Harbor adapter
default. The selected verifier budget is 30 minutes total, including clean
execution capped at 900 seconds. These are Marin protocol choices, not
paper-specified agent deadlines.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Snowball RL recipes force NCCL onto socket transport while their jobs request InfiniBand resources. Multi-node collectives therefore bypass the fast cross-node interconnect, and one production run stopped with a socket-transport NCCL error.

The resolved launch config for the `2026.11.16.51` long-loop RL run (cluster `cw-rno2a`, 32 nodes x 8 H100, attempt `cb784b53b8fd`) sets:

```yaml
task_env:
  NCCL_IB_DISABLE: '1'
  NCCL_NET: Socket
  NCCL_SOCKET_FAMILY: AF_INET
```

The same job requested 256 GPUs and 256 `rdma/ib` devices. At RL update 4, a Megatron context-parallel ALLTOALL on NCCL 2.29.7 failed:

```
ncclInvalidUsage: NET/Socket : peer 10.168.206.29<44220> message truncated : receiving 941711616 bytes instead of 32
```

The NCCL watchdog aborted the worker with SIGABRT. The run completed 3 RL updates, below its budget, and produced no final checkpoint.

Commit [410e9c25](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/410e9c25a8) ("Use IPv4 socket transport for Snowball inventory smoke", 2026-10-20) added the three variables to `experiments/post_training/snowball_inventory_smoke.py` and records no reason. Later commits copied them into the recipes below. The commit records no reason. Logs show that the inventory smoke it unblocked (`2026.10.20.3`, cw-us-east-02a) failed with `NET/IB IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR(12)` on `mlx5_0` (table below). The same error occurred in the July 2026 B200 bring-up (logbooks B200MFU-020/-028). No later recipe re-tested InfiniBand before it copied the override.

The main quick-loop recipe forces NCCL onto sockets; [#11178](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11178) removes that override but currently conflicts with main. issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
🤖 Daytona sandboxes created through Shellbox from a Dockerfile that copies local files (`COPY workspace/ /app/`) can start with every copied file present but 0 bytes long. The build succeeds and no error is reported. Shellbox is Marin's sandbox interface; Harbor evals use its Daytona backend to build each task's image in Daytona's hosted sandboxes. Both of its build modes are affected: `snapshot` (the default) and `declarative` ([image_build](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cc951767f350beb828ad1d3ec71a6a859fa8eaed/docs/harbor-integration.md#L102)).

Empty files can turn into false results. In a 20-task Harbor eval of the Aider Polyglot benchmark on Marin's Daytona eval org, the 11 C++, Go and Java sandboxes started with empty workspace files, including `CMakeLists.txt` and `gradlew`. All 8 C++ and Java trials scored as passes because their test step built and ran nothing.

Cause: Shellbox passes Daytona `Image.from_dockerfile(...)` ([snapshot.py#L146](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cc951767f350beb828ad1d3ec71a6a859fa8eaed/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/snapshot.py#L146)). The pinned Daytona SDK (`daytona==0.200.2`, `daytona/_async/object_storage.py`) then uploads each `COPY` source to an object store shared by the whole Daytona org, as `{org}/{key}/context.tar`, and skips the upload when that key already exists. The key is an MD5 of the archive path and of each file's path and contents, with contents read through symlinks. The uploaded tar, however, stores symlinks as links. If anyone in the org once uploaded the same files as symlinks, the store holds a tar of dangling links under the key of the real files, and every later build with that key gets empty files. The key also depends on the order `os.walk` lists files, so two hosts building identical files can compute different keys and get different results.

Marin's Daytona eval org holds such objects. For the task `aider_polyglot/polyglot_cpp_clock` in [harbor-datasets](https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor-datasets/tree/f30b14415dd733c83627204bad0af69a89ceb46f/datasets/aider_polyglot/polyglot_cpp_clock) (commit f30b144), the key for byte-sorted file order, `8b55826da2064ff505c84dd21f3cbd5c`, holds a tar of symlinks uploaded on 2025-11-26, while the objects stored under four other file orders hold the real files. Among the 20 tasks in the run above, each of the 11 C++, Go and Java tasks has such an object.

Reproduce:
1. Create `ctx/Dockerfile` containing `FROM python:3.12-slim` and `COPY workspace/ /app/`, and `ctx/workspace/payload.txt` with contents no earlier build has used.
2. Create `other/workspace/payload.txt` as a symlink to a file with the same contents. Store it as the SDK does, with `AsyncObjectStorage.upload("other/workspace/", org_id, "workspace/")`.
3. Create a sandbox from `ctx` with [`DaytonaMachineFactory`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cc951767f350beb828ad1d3ec71a6a859fa8eaed/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L534) in either build mode and run `wc -c /app/payload.txt`. It reports 0 bytes. Without step 2, it reports the file's size.

Expected: a sandbox built from local files contains those files, whatever the org's object store already holds.

Dockerfiles that copy no local files are unaffected. Earlier Daytona results for tasks whose Dockerfiles do copy files, and snapshots built from those tasks, may have used empty files. The SDK behavior should also be reported to Daytona.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`DaytonaMachineFactory.create()` routes snapshot builds through `ensure_snapshot()` and declarative builds through `daytona_image()`; both reach `Image.from_dockerfile()`. With the pinned Daytona 0.200.2 SDK, the object key hashes dereferenced file bytes while the uploaded tar preserves symlinks, so a cached tar can have different contents from the files that produced its key. A snapshot built from that tar is then reused under Shellbox's content-derived snapshot name. I found no open PR for #11595 or this cache collision.

**Relevant code**
- [`snapshot.py#L136-L148`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a8d563e2fca1a3809747a7defb8d833c5598ab40/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/snapshot.py#L136-L148) — snapshot identity and SDK image construction
- [`snapshot.py#L181-L195`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a8d563e2fca1a3809747a7defb8d833c5598ab40/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/snapshot.py#L181-L195) — existing snapshots bypass a rebuild
- [`machine.py#L620-L627`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a8d563e2fca1a3809747a7defb8d833c5598ab40/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L620-L627) — both build modes
- [`image.py#L87-L103`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a8d563e2fca1a3809747a7defb8d833c5598ab40/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/image.py#L87-L103) — Shellbox's context identity records symlink type

# Proposed Fix

1. Check the current compatible Daytona SDK for this collision. If it remains, report a minimal reproduction upstream and change its object key to hash a canonical, sorted manifest of the *archived* entries, including file type, symlink target, and regular-file contents. Version the object key namespace so already poisoned objects cannot be reused.
2. Pin Shellbox to the fixed SDK and add a regression for equal-byte regular files versus symlinks and for different filesystem traversal orders. Version Shellbox's Dockerfile snapshot identity once so existing bad snapshots are rebuilt; leave registry-image identities alone.
3. Validate both `snapshot` and `declarative` builds in an isolated Daytona org with the issue's reproduction, then rerun the affected 20-task eval and inspect copied file sizes before accepting scores. Treat the eight reported C++/Java passes and any snapshots derived from these tasks as invalid until that rerun. Use prebuilt registry images for affected tasks in the meantime.

This is an experiment-tracking issue for launching the cleaned Datakit SFT mixture (67B/2B-active, step 157,000, 80% SFT / 20% replay, 2,000 steps) on a non-preemptible v4-2048. spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Generation-only evaluation with TP1/PP1 and DP16/EP16 fails before vLLM actor creation when `trainer.placement.colocate_all=true`. The engine factory rejects the four-host layout with `a DP/EP group must be node-local`, although the launcher accepts this layout and the factory supports verified cross-host EP workers.

Reproduce:
1. Use `skyrl_train.entrypoints.main_generate` with one TP1/PP1, DP16/EP16 vLLM engine on four four-GPU hosts in one NVLink domain.
2. Set `trainer.placement.colocate_all=true` so the generation run uses exactly the 16 inference GPUs.
3. Start the evaluation. The shared placement group sets `use_hybrid_engine=true`; `verify_workers` becomes false, so `_validate_node_local_dp_ranks` rejects the engine before actor creation.

Expected: generation-only workers use the verified cross-host EP path, including host, physical GPU UUID and DP/EP rank checks. Training sleep behavior and unsupported-layout checks must remain active.

`main_base.py` already disables engine sleep for generation. The factory also excludes every shared placement group from worker verification, which incorrectly treats the generation group as sleeping training. The same condition exists on main at `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py`. The failed attempt reached this guard before policy weight loading or CUDA graph capture, so the evidence does not indicate a checkpoint or PIECEWISE failure.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
## Research

`main_generate` passes a shared placement group with engine sleep disabled. The factory excludes every shared group from worker verification, so `cross_node_ep` is false and the node-local DP guard rejects the four-host layout before actor creation. The existing placement verifier can map shared bundles across hosts and checks worker host, GPU UUID, and DP/EP ranks.

**Relevant code**
- [`main_base.py#L199-L212`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py#L199-L212) — generation disables engine sleep
- [`ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L603-L627`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L603-L627) — shared group suppresses verification
- [`ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L772-L780`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/ray_wrapped_inference_engine.py#L772-L780) — node-local guard rejects DP ranks
- [`placement.py#L110-L143`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inference_engines/placement.py#L110-L143) — shared bundle mapping

## Proposed Fix

Allow TP1 workers in a shared placement group to use verification when engine sleep is disabled. Keep sleeping colocated training on its current path, and add regression coverage for the verification decision and cross-host placement checks.

spillover_issues.author: davidlundgren
spillover_issues.body:
Behaviors in the 10.05 SFT model's eval outputs that trace to data flaws listed in #11188. Measured on ~72k stored outputs and agent steps; method and scripts in [marin-logbooks#60](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/60).

| Pathology | Incidence (10.05) | Pass-rate lift if removed (95% CI) | Suspected source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Token soup (mixed-script gibberish in agent steps) | 18% TBLite, 22.5% TB2 trials; 0.3% of steps <4k ctx, 4.6% >40k | +1.7 TBLite (0.2, 3.4); +1.9 TB2 (0.4, 4.1) | Hypothesis: binary/pickle dumps in long-context replay | Untested; needs long agent evals |
| Success claimed right after a visible error | 9.7% TBLite, 3.7% TB2 trials | +0.4 (−1.1, 1.7); +0.6 (0, 1.5) | Agent traces ending in unverified success claims | Untested |
| Wrong-language answer or stray foreign words | 0.1–2.5% of outputs | Not estimated | Multilingual v1 | Untested |
| gpt-oss typography (U+202F, U+2011) | 43% MMLU-Pro; 3–12% math/IF | 0 | Teacher style in math, finance, proofs | Fixed by normalization in marin-logbooks#60; no accuracy change |

Lifts are upper bounds: a trial that avoids one pathology can fail another way.

**Next:** token soup is the only row with a measurable lift. Test it first: locate the binary dumps in replay, filter them, train 100 steps, then score TBLite/TB2 at the trained checkpoint.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

Token soup appears in 18% of TBLite and 22.5% of TB2 trials, but its proposed cause in replay remains untested. The 5.3M-token pickle and 3.0M-token gzip examples in [#11188](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11188) exceed the candidate pipeline's 262,144-token row limit; the audit alone does not show whether comparable bytes reached the historical 10.05 training positions. [PR #11547](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11547) already contains replay labeling, scoring, filters, and retention receipts, but has not run against the production manifests or submitted training.

**Relevant code**
- [10.05 mix](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ce7c77abcb0ada792cd6d76ba3d80db74c33a859/experiments/grug_sft/special_token_full_ab_grouped.py#L22-L33) — historical run and store manifest.
- [Replay calibration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/calibrate_replay.py#L54-L105) — cutoff and held-out metrics.
- [Candidate replay gates](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/exp3_build.py#L152-L171) — context limit and per-row decisions.
- [Replay scoring](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b89bba1c3f11ae14b23954090c8d299b1517e61/experiments/sft_new_mix/exp3_build.py#L253-L296) — calibrated score and drop receipt.

# Proposed Fix

1. Resolve the frozen 10.05 store manifest and replay source revisions. Trace the cited pickle/gzip rows and a sample of token-soup-like rows through packing to the positions actually trained. Record row IDs, token ranges, and replay share; keep the historical stores as the control.
2. Use the replay calibration and decision receipts in #11547 for a **binary/pickle/gzip-specific** selection on a held-out labeled sample, including clean structured-data controls. Report false drops, recall, and retained tokens by replay source and length tier. Its current held-out junkgate result (1/12 low-value rows recalled; 2/67 natural rows dropped) is too small to justify an unreviewed broad replay cutoff.
3. Freeze one filter version, then train 100-step control and treatment arms from the same starting checkpoint with identical optimizer settings, seed, trained-token positions, and replay allocation. Replace dropped replay positions from eligible replay rows in the same strata and publish both manifests and receipts.
4. Run TBLite and TB2 on the same tasks and seeds at both checkpoints. Report token-soup incidence by context-length bin, pass rates, paired confidence intervals, and any regressions. Treat 100 steps as a screening experiment; choose a longer run only if the observed reduction survives manual review and the paired results support it.

The data selection belongs with #11547; this issue should track the causal training and evaluation result.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Pi trials with a non-root task user fail before agent execution when the root uploader owns Pi's temporary runtime files.

Reproduce:
1. Use a Linux Harbor environment with a non-root default user and sticky `/tmp` (mode 1777).
2. Start the installed Pi agent with `api_base` and `api_key` set (values need not be valid; do not print them).
3. Observe `Operation not permitted` when the task user removes `/tmp/harbor-pi-endpoint.env` or `/tmp/harbor-pi-context-budget.js`.

Expected: the configured task user can read and remove its staged runtime files, with mode 0600.

Main `f5d3c85f9e` uploads these files without assigning their owner in `vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py` (`_stage_endpoint_env` and `_stage_context_budget_extension`). A regional Linux trial reproduced the failure. Assigning those staged files to the task user and mode 0600 allowed the next real trial to run.

Source: [Pi staging](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f5d3c85f9e/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L571).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`Pi.run()` uploads the endpoint environment and context-budget extension before executing as the task user. A root-owned upload at a fixed path in sticky `/tmp` cannot be removed by that user.

**Relevant code**
- [`pi.py#L572-L619`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/530487a57475961cf006a7c7d2a8b973e33169ab/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py#L572-L619) — staging in the existing PR
- [`base.py#L433-L445`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/83ab8b902ec957bb58219e9d1a96db16c4619938/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/base.py#L433-L445) — agent-user execution

# Proposed Fix

[PR #11530](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11530) already replaces the fixed paths with a task-user-owned private directory and cleans it on normal exit. Its uploads do not set file ownership or `0600` mode, so that requirement remains open. I flagged the gap on the PR and am handing this issue to that existing change.

comments.author: yonromai
comments.body:
🤖 The remaining ownership and `0600` requirements are addressed by #11530 at [5def31ba](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/5def31ba1b429d08f464f9e2ffda922787975d27). Pi assigns each successful staged upload to the task user before it is consumed.

A native Linux check with separate root uploader and non-root task identities reproduces the earlier read failure, then verifies task ownership, mode `0600`, read access and cleanup for hosted-provider registration and agent execution. The private directories remain outside collected logs. #11530 includes `Fixes #11610` and remains unmerged.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Not actionable as written — the described fields do not exist, and the references don't match.**

I checked the current codebase against every concrete claim here and none of them hold:

- **No `run_with_scripts` (field 7).** [`EnvironmentConfig`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto#L479-L489) has only `env_vars = 2`, `setup_scripts = 6`, and `reserved 1, 3, 4, 5`. There is no field 7, and `run_with_scripts` appears nowhere in the repo.
- **`setup_scripts` (field 6) is the current mechanism, not a compatibility shim.** It is the resolved setup list the worker runs before the command, consumed at runtime by [`entrypoint.py`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/entrypoint.py#L30) and published as `IRIS_JOB_SETUP_SCRIPTS` by [`env.py`](../blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/env.py#L236). Removing it would break setup execution and child-env inheritance.
- **No `IRIS_JOB_RUN_WITH_SCRIPTS`** env var, and no "environment layers" concept anywhere in the code.
- **The references don't line up.** PR #8639 is "[grug] Bound hero loader cache and add native heap profiles" and #8506 is "Hero Run / Ongoing Status" — neither concerns environment setup fields.
- Separately, even on the issue's own terms, removal is gated to no earlier than 2026-09-08, and today is 2026-08-25.

To make this actionable, please confirm which repository and branch the field numbering refers to and correct the cross-references. If the intent is a different cleanup on the real `EnvironmentConfig`, state the exact fields, the replacement mechanism, and a definition of done against `lib/iris/src/iris/rpc/job.proto` as it stands. I did not open a PR.

## 10/05 Micro210 baseline

Evaluation-only entry for the frozen 10/05 model; this does not introduce a new SFT or RL training recipe.

Micro210 is Marin’s mixed reasoning, knowledge, coding and agentic evaluation suite.
This recipe supports 200 distinct tasks across 20 sources (Tau3 excluded), expanded to 440 assignments, including 100 Pi assignments.

## Model and evaluation policy

Model: [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05/tree/ac60d9401820953943f5a56e06f36e13c86b12d6), immutable revision `ac60d9401820953943f5a56e06f36e13c86b12d6`. The three runs evaluate this same model in existing region-local storage, with no additional training.

The runtime separately selects [marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools](https://huggingface.co/marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools/tree/3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09), revision `3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09`, with no explicit template override and thinking enabled. The model’s embedded tokenizer provenance is not the selected runtime tools revision.

Current harness: 16 global Harbor slots (four rollout workers × four), one 8 H100 policy worker (TP1/DP8/EP8, max_num_seqs 8) and an independent 8 H100 M3 judge (TP8). Policy/judge caps are 21,600 s; root cap is 25,200 s. Native Pi 0.87; context 65,536, 16,384 generated tokens per turn, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95. Compilation and CUDA graphs remain enabled. These role budgets are not asserted identical to every historical recipe in this issue.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Streamed SkyRL policy loading enables RunAI distributed loading without a finite host-memory limit when the recipe omits loader settings. A 535B BF16 policy with TP1/PP1 and DP16/EP16 reached 910.94 GB of 955.71 GB host RAM during startup; four EngineCore processes each used 191–197 GB. Ray killed a serving actor at its 0.95 threshold, and the remaining ranks failed engine initialization.

Reproduce:
1. Launch a large streamed policy with four inference ranks per host and no explicit `generator.engine_init_kwargs.model_loader_extra_config`.
2. `create_ray_wrapped_inference_engines_from_config` in `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py` supplies `distributed=true` but no `memory_limit`.
3. RunAI model streamer 0.16.1 changes an unset `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT` to `-1` for distributed streaming. Loading can exhaust host RAM before serving starts.

Expected: the launch requires or derives a finite loader memory budget that accounts for concurrent workers on each host. Keep Ray memory protection enabled.

The pinned vLLM loader accepts explicit `distributed`, `concurrency` and `memory_limit` fields. The existing NVL72 training recipe uses distributed=false, concurrency=4 and an 8 GiB memory limit. The affected evaluation recipe omitted those fields; reusing the bounded training settings is the immediate recipe fix. The shared main default remains a separate correction.

The pinned loader source is [runai_streamer_loader.py](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader.py). The model-streamer dependency and version are pinned in `vendor/skyrl/uv.lock`. Startup passed the prior placement guard and reported DP/EP ranks 0–15 before the memory kill.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`create_ray_wrapped_inference_engines_from_config` selects distributed RunAI streaming for a policy with `source_uri`, but supplies no `memory_limit` when the recipe omits loader settings. The pinned vLLM loader sets `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT` only for an explicit value, leaving RunAI 0.16.1 to use its unbounded distributed default. The [Mochi training recipe in #11321](https://github.com/yonromai/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L147-L154) uses an 8 GiB per-worker cap; that recipe is not on `main`.

**Relevant code**
- [`main_base.py#L165-L171`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7ecd2a9ad2493b79bffb26a7366d3ce92ea4af1d/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/entrypoints/main_base.py#L165-L171) — streaming loader configuration.
- [`runai_streamer_loader.py#L46-L68`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader.py#L46-L68) — explicit limit forwarded to RunAI.

# Proposed Fix

The launch path passes `model_loader_extra_config` to the pinned vLLM loader, which leaves the RunAI limit unset when the config omits it. Set a finite 8 GiB per-worker default for streamed policies, preserve explicit finite limits, and reject an explicit unbounded limit; add a CPU regression for the launcher configuration. This caps four concurrent inference workers at 32 GiB of streamer buffers per host while retaining Ray memory protection.

## TL;DR

Ablations on Snowball (the 10/05 SFT model) to choose SFT and RL settings for the Mochi 535B post-training run. Each experiment has a 1 h version and an 8 h version. Most backlog items have not run yet; current results are under Status.

## Description

Snowball is a smaller Grug MoE with the same post-training stack as Mochi. Each experiment changes one setting of the SFT or RL recipe (data, optimizer, loss mask, precision, tool format, RL task choice) and compares it against a matched control. The arms are read out with Micro210, BFCL ×5 and a retention panel. Experiments that look useful are then checked on Mochi.

Issue 11177 made the long loop runnable from the 10/05 SFT. Issue 11337 tracks run-ready Snowball recipes and Micro eval scores. Issue 11531 tracks Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find which recipe settings change Snowball's agentic and tool-use scores enough to carry into Mochi's next SFT/RL stage.

## Sub-issues

Each result is posted on its own issue:
- Snowball long-loop SFT on TPU v4: issue 11531
- Malformed JSON in nested Pi edit calls: issue 11536
- SFT optimizer, Muon-H vs Adam (C150 vs O150): issue 11537
- TMax data, with vs without: issue 11539
- RL samples per prompt: issue 11594
- Mochi BFCL ×5 versus Snowball models: issue 11538

## Status

- **Tool-call format:** see the sub-issue. Malformed nested `edit` calls end more than half of Snowball's SWE trials. An SFT slice of valid nested edits (E12) is trained but not yet read out.
- **SFT optimizer (C150 vs O150):** BFCL ×5 favours Muon-H (30.24% vs 24.55–24.72%, one run each); Micro210 pending. See issue 11537.
- **TMax pair:** held-out TMax loss falls sharply; BFCL ×5 falls vs control. Micro210 pending. See issue 11539.
- **Mochi BFCL ×5 (Pi agent, 123 tasks):** 450/615 record score under the configured retry rule; 449 first-attempt wins, one first-attempt reward unavailable after a timeout.

## Links

* Logbook:
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

- 2026-11-16: Flat edit tool ruled out for reported benchmarks and the default harness. The fix for malformed edits goes on the model side (SFT data).

The E12 one-hour arms also await readout; [#11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536) tracks their nested-edit hypothesis. The two published [long-loop recipes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337) changed training recipes and have different scoring coverage, so their aggregate scores do not isolate an ablation effect.

Plan:
1. For each SFT or RL setting, pin a control and one-setting treatment at the one-hour and eight-hour budgets. Match the starting checkpoint, source and data revisions outside the tested change, task IDs, seeds, Pi harness, and eval policy. Preserve the consumed configs and checkpoint revisions.
2. Finish the pending C150/O150/TMax and E12 one-hour Micro210 readouts first. Compare matching task IDs and report scored/unscored counts, per-benchmark and aggregate deltas, BFCL ×5, and the retention panel. Include malformed nested-edit rates for E12. Use [#11536's gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536): at least a 50% rate reduction against its control with no Micro210 or retention loss.
3. Advance arms with a positive paired agentic/tool-use result and no retention regression to matched eight-hour controls. Repeat the same panels, report uncertainty and incomplete coverage, and record null or adverse results. Check surviving settings on Mochi before selecting its SFT/RL recipe.
4. Keep an arm table here with the changed setting, control and treatment pins, both budget readouts, BFCL and retention results, and the carry/drop decision. Add each run-ready recipe, exact data mix, Micro policy, immutable checkpoint, and archive receipts to [#11337](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337).

## Metric definitions

Equal-20 is recomputed from the 20 native per-source avg_score fields. Those fields include excluded assignments in their denominators. Available-only columns omit excluded scores and therefore use different denominators.

Task-equivalent differences are n × (arm mean − parent run 1 mean), summed over sources. Here n counts assignments, not necessarily distinct task identities. Fractional graders produce fractional task-equivalents, not additional integer wins. No individual task outcomes have been paired.

BFCL /10 is the native score mass for the ten-assignment Micro slice. C150 has five known score units, nine scored assignments and one unknown outcome: its assigned score bounds are 5–6 /10. The regional parent has seven known score units over nine scored assignments plus one unknown: assigned bounds 7–8 /10. This slice is not the earlier 123-task ×5 BFCL evaluation.

The parent repeat has seven unknown outcomes: one BixBench and six TB2. The first parent reports 440/440 scored and zero excluded. Both have complete native aggregate dumps; the repeat does not have complete scored outcomes. The two runs use the same configured seed and recipe, not independent training seeds or proven matched random streams.

## Evidence boundaries

All 14 scored rows have reviewed native aggregates and terminal resource accounting. For the earlier seven rows, individual source files were metadata-listed, not independently checked for exact assigned-UID membership, raw exceptions or file hashes. Each current TMax and cw-rno2a dump has 21 streamed and hashed files, 440 unique expected UID strings, and all 20 source means/counts/exclusions reconciled under the frozen UID-source mapping. That reduced extraction does not independently prove the actual source-file-to-UID/task join. Produced suite artifacts match the 440-row reference bytes and order where checked; that does not attest live runtime consumption. Native completion, archive membership and trace capture are separate evidence.

Requested H100-hours are physical-attempt resource envelopes, not utilization, invoices or Pod/provider-release timing. Native success is not broad-suite green or evidence that the unresolved import failures are harmless.

The two parent judge workers and brokers each had only A0. Their final preemption_count of one accompanies terminal KILLED cleanup after the policy child finished; no native restart gap was found. This does not prove continuous HTTP health or explain the repeat's seven exclusions. The bound vllm_server.py is identical between those runs; a different file in the current checkout is not a run-to-run source change or a deployed-byte readback.

The old RNO control run used eight slots and three-hour child caps. The old TMax arm failed and yielded a conservative recovered subset of 437/440: available macro 52.39%, pooled 44.99%, three unknown. There was no complete native aggregate for that arm. Neither result fills a current-harness row. The superseded failed parent recovery is not used here.

The two current TMax runs bind the original cw-us-east-02a exports without copying: arm 134,181,708,393 B; control 134,181,708,404 B. Both have 87 HF objects and 39 weight shards. Fresh metadata and header checks are not a new full tensor-payload parity audit.

The two Micro210 repetitions per export and regional parent all have successful roots and policies, seven terminal jobs and seven observed A0 attempts per evaluation. Judge workers and brokers were KILLED after policy completion. No retry or continuous-health inference follows from the one-attempt observations. W&B in-run metrics and teacher-closeness NLL are not Micro210.

Accepted failure/preemption/job-wide retry limits are explicit: root 0/0/0; policy 0/1000/0; judge 1/10/1; broker 0/1000/0; prepare-model 1/100/0; prepare_micro and verify_ready_inputs each 0/100/0. All 39 same-named shard hashes recorded in the two export manifests differ between the RL exports and from the parent's retained verified shard hashes. comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 ## Finding: the long-loop SFT ablations used a different optimizer grouping from 10/05 and Mochi

Found on 2026-11-17 while preparing an arm that restores the 10/05 optimizer state: the saved state did not fit the optimizer that the long-loop SFT code builds.

## What differs

| Parameter family | 10/05 (saved optimizer state, logged config) | Mochi SFT (sealed source, hero-EP optimizer) | Long-loop SFT ablations (bound source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stacked expert `w_gate` / `w_up` / `w_down` (4-D) | MuonH | MuonH | **Adam** |
| Stacked `rms_attn` / `rms_mlp` scales (2-D) | Adam | Adam | **MuonH** |
| Shared expert weights (3-D) | MuonH | MuonH | MuonH |
| Gradient clipping | none | not compared | **1.0** (E12 config) |

## Cause

The long-loop `sft.py` imports the generic `experiments/grug/moe/optimizer.py`. Its MuonH rule accepts only 2-D and 3-D weights and has no rule that sends RMSNorm scales to Adam. With stacked blocks the 4-D expert weights fall through to Adam and the 2-D stacked norm scales go to MuonH. The June TPU optimizer implementation that the 10/05 model card links to, which is consistent with that run's saved optimizer slots and logged config, and the hero-EP optimizer in the sealed Mochi source both handle the stacked case explicitly (RMSNorm scales to Adam, 2-D to 4-D weights to MuonH). The generic file at `main` commit `18ae01ee42` is byte-identical to the one the ablations used.

## Runs affected

- **Affected (bound source and published consumed configs; worker import bytes not separately attested):** the E12 all-weights and general-only arms, the TMax arm and its control, C150, and the low-learning-rate replay rerun of 2026-11-17.
- **Related code, swapped families not trained:** the E12 attention-and-head-only arm freezes the expert and norm families, so the swap does not act on it.
- **Not affected:** Mochi SFT through step 400,407 (from its sealed source, not a fresh worker attestation); O150 (plain Adam by design); the RL arms (Megatron AdamW).

## What this does and does not show

- The E12 all-weights and general-only arms and the TMax arm and control used this grouping in their bound source. None is a matched test of the 10/05 optimizer set-up.
- It is a candidate cause of that drop. It is **not** shown to be the cause; no run with the corrected grouping has been evaluated yet.
- The 10/05 grouping is established from its logged optimizer config (`rmsnorm_to_adam=true`, no clipping) and its saved optimizer slots. The exact commit that run was launched from is not recorded in its W&B run.

## Next

1. A replay-only arm on 10/05 (15 updates, fresh optimizer state, learning rate 5e-6) with the 10/05 grouping and no clipping. The grouping change labels all 27 parameter leaves of the model the same way as the 10/05 optimizer state.
2. The same arm with the uncorrected grouping finished training on 2026-11-17 and is being evaluated; the pair gives the comparison.
3. A fix for the generic optimizer, or a switch of the long-loop SFT code to the hero-EP optimizer, follows as a PR.

spillover_issues.body:
## Summary

The campaign's Daytona environment kwargs include `trial_attempt_timeout_sec` for every Daytona task. The shellbox Daytona path accepts the argument (it selects `ProviderWaitPolicy.JOB` over `PHASE`), but the TaskSpec trial path rejected it as unknown:

```
File "vendor/harbor/src/harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py", line 522, in _prepare
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported TaskSpec Daytona arguments: {sorted(unknown)}")
ValueError: Unsupported TaskSpec Daytona arguments: ['trial_attempt_timeout_sec']
```

Every TaskSpec Daytona attempt therefore failed at trial prepare. In the difficulty rounds this surfaced as 22 daytona-heavy sources recording ~600 `infrastructure` attempts each across two rounds (v18d, v19) with zero scored coverage (`awaiting_scored_coverage`), while native-harbor Daytona sources measured normally.

## Impact

- Any caller passing the documented Daytona environment kwargs from the campaign flip (provisioning + trial_attempt_timeout_sec) to a TaskSpec task fails 100% of attempts.
- The per-attempt timeout itself is unaffected: `TrialConfig.trial_attempt_timeout_sec` enforces it independently; the environment kwarg only selects the provider wait policy, and the TaskSpec path pins `ProviderWaitPolicy.JOB` unconditionally.

## Fix

Consume the argument in the TaskSpec Daytona branch (the pinned JOB policy already implements its semantics) instead of rejecting it: vendored `harbor/trial/taskcompendium.py`, with a regression trial test asserting the attempt prepares and grades with the kwarg present. Landed on the atlas-env-audit integration branch as 3e2f590278 (test: `test_declarative_task_spec_accepts_attempt_timeout_argument`).

## Evidence

- v19 round: s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.18.2/small-v19 — per-attempt trial-artifacts exception.txt showing the traceback above for all 100 tasks of each affected source.

Second root cause found in the same failure chain, fixed separately: even with the TaskSpec whitelist resolved, every Daytona attempt still failed at client creation — `ValueError: Daytona requires an explicit api_key, api_url and target` (`shellbox/backends/daytona/connection.py`). The campaign's trial worker built `HostCapabilities` from an **empty** environment snapshot (`execute_trial` passed `{}` to `host_capabilities_from_environment`, since the trial-runner landing 5ba55ccb03), so the connection never carried the mapped `DAYTONA_API_KEY`/`DAYTONA_API_URL`/`DAYTONA_TARGET` the worker inherits. The native shellbox path failed the same way — meaning Daytona-backend sources never scored in the difficulty campaign rounds, not just TaskSpec ones.

Fix: resolve capabilities from the worker's own environment (`worker_host_capabilities`), landed as bb10af1189 on the atlas-env-audit integration branch with a regression test asserting the connection resolves from `DAYTONA_*` env vars and that empty snapshots still produce the incomplete connection. Evidence: v20 (s3://marin-rno2a/marin/rl-data/atlas/difficulty/2026.11.18.6/small-v20) — the TaskSpec sources passed the whitelist fix and failed ~900 more infrastructure attempts at `client_factory`.
